findings.title: 29 assert-guarded structural checks vanish under python -O: corewise ops silently truncate, T3 * wrong-shape array silently broadcasts
findings.claim: Structural consistency is enforced by assert(...) at 29 sites (corewise.py:61,62,84,85,210,211,241,242; backend/ranks.py:111,112,342,353,354,537,538; backend/t3_linalg.py:61,117,195,258; backend/t3_operations.py:296,297; backend/common.py:346,352,369,375,390,396; backend/probing.py:1514,1515; tucker_tensor_train.py:2023). Under python -O these are stripped, contradicting the house rule that structural problems always error: corewise_add/sub/dot on length-mismatched trees return a silently truncated result (zip), and x * ndarray of the wrong shape returns a broadcast dense array; others degrade to IndexError/ValueError from numpy. Without -O they raise a bare AssertionError with no message.
findings.evidence: asserts_under_O.py: without -O every case -> AssertionError (empty message); with -O: corewise_add len mismatch -> RETURNED tuple len 2 (inputs had 3 vs 2 elements); corewise_dot len mismatch -> RETURNED float64; x * np.ones((4,5,1)) -> RETURNED (4,5,6) ndarray; t3_sum axis=5 -> IndexError; compute_minimal_ranks bad tt len -> IndexError; t3_add stack mismatch -> numpy ValueError.
findings.repro_output: python -O active (asserts stripped): True / corewise_add len mismatch -> RETURNED tuple len 2: [(2,), (2,)] / x * ndarray wrong shape -> RETURNED ((4, 5, 6), 'ndarray')
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the structural assert(...) calls with explicit raise ValueError(message) (they are cheap integer/shape checks).
findings.supported_path: Any structural misuse when the interpreter runs with -O / PYTHONOPTIMIZE.
findings.related_known: map_core_ragged.md flagged the ~28 asserts as a candidate; this confirms the behaviour change.

findings.title: jax absent: randn(use_jax=True) is a bare NameError (beyond get_backend); to_jax()/load(use_jax=True) silently return numpy
findings.claim: common.randn does jnp.array(np.random.randn(...)) with jnp unbound when jax is not installed, so TuckerTensorTrain.randn(..., use_jax=True) and UniformTuckerTensorTrain.randn(..., use_jax=True) raise NameError: name 'jnp' is not defined -- a second NameError site independent of the known get_backend one. Separately, common.py:102 sets to_jax = np.array when jax is absent, so x.to_jax(), TuckerTensorTrain.load(f, use_jax=True) and tree_to_jax return numpy arrays with no error, contradicting the to_jax docstring ('Convert core arrays ... to Jax arrays') and load's 'Cores are jax arrays if True'. newton_cg(use_jit=True) by contrast raises a clear ValueError.
findings.evidence: jax_absent.py (sys.modules['jax']=None): jax_available = False; T3.randn(use_jax=True) FAIL NameError: name 'jnp' is not defined; UT3.randn(use_jax=True) FAIL NameError; to_jax() OK TuckerTensorTrain (numpy cores); T3.load(use_jax=True) OK TuckerTensorTrain (numpy). jax_absent_optim.py: newton_cg use_jit=True -> ValueError: use_jit=True requires jax (install the t3toolbox[jax] extra)...
findings.repro_output: T3.randn(use_jax=True) [expect clear error] FAIL NameError: name 'jnp' is not defined / to_jax() OK TuckerTensorTrain / T3.load(use_jax=True) [expect clear error] OK TuckerTensorTrain
findings.proposed_fix: Add one _require_jax(what) helper that raises ImportError('... install the t3toolbox[jax] extra') and call it from get_backend(use_jax=True), randn(use_jax=True) and to_jax when jax_available is False.
findings.supported_path: pip install t3toolbox without the [jax] extra, then TuckerTensorTrain.randn(..., use_jax=True) or x.to_jax().
findings.related_known: dev/HANDOFF.md backlog 'get_backend raises a bare NameError: name jnp is not defined' -- this is broader (common.randn) plus the silent to_jax fallback.

findings.title: TuckerTensorTrain has no __rmul__: 2.0 * x raises while x * 2.0 works; the uniform and tangent classes define it
findings.claim: TuckerTensorTrain defines __mul__ only; scalar * x raises TypeError. UniformTuckerTensorTrain, T3Tangent and UT3Tangent all set __rmul__ = __mul__, so the ragged keystone is the odd one out.
findings.evidence: matrix_ragged_t3.out: every structure, mul_scalar -> np ERR TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'TuckerTensorTrain' (jax and jit identical); x * 2.0 works everywhere.
findings.repro_output: T3 d1 () mul_scalar np ERR TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'float' and 'TuckerTensorTrain'
findings.proposed_fix: Add __rmul__ delegating to __mul__ for the scalar case (and keep the ndarray case asymmetric or document it).
findings.supported_path: 2.0 * x for a TuckerTensorTrain x.
findings.related_known: Known-list item '__mul__ dead use_jax param' is the same method; this is a different defect.

findings.title: Stacked t3_orthogonal_representations rotates the t3svd Tucker factors, so T3FrameWeights.from_t3weights(T3Weights.from_t3svd(x)) is applied in the wrong gauge (docs/weighting.md recipe)
findings.claim: The weighting page pairs frame, _ = t3_orthogonal_representations(x) with W = T3FrameWeights.from_t3weights(T3Weights.from_t3svd(x)); the sigma-weights are per-coordinate in the t3svd gauge. For an unstacked t3svd output the re-orthogonalized frame's up cores equal the t3svd factors up to sign, but for stack_shape=(2,) they do not (the stacked sweep rotates the Tucker factors), so the sigma-weights land on rotated coordinates; this surfaces as the absorbed tangent differing between numpy and jax on identical input (relerr 0.7 ragged d2 (2,); 0.09/1.4 uniform d2 ()), i.e. the weighted result is gauge-dependent on a path the docs present as canonical.
findings.evidence: inline check (lane log): stack () -> frame up cores == t3svd tucker cores up to sign: numpy True jax True; stack (2,) -> False False (numpy vs jax frames identical). matrix_ragged_tangent.out: TANGENT d2 (2,) tangent_absorb_weights np/jax MISMATCH relerr 7.04e-01; matrix_uniform.out: UNIFORM d2 () tangent_absorb_weights MISMATCH 9.26e-02, ufv_absorb_weights MISMATCH 1.41e+00.
findings.repro_output: stack (2,) | numpy vs jax frames identical: True | frame up cores == t3svd tucker cores up to sign: numpy False jax False ||| TANGENT d2 (2,) tangent_absorb_weights np/jax MISMATCH relerr 7.04e-01
findings.proposed_fix: Document that from_t3svd weights pair with the t3svd gauge and build the frame with T3Frame.from_t3(xs) (no re-orthogonalization) in that recipe; or make t3_orthogonal_representations leave already-orthonormal Tucker factors untouched (stacked path included). To confirm fully: compare weighted_norm against the dense sigma-weighted norm for a stacked xs.
findings.supported_path: docs/weighting.md lines 79-82 recipe applied to a stacked (C != ()) point, or to a uniform point.
findings.related_known: docs/contributor/weighted_internals.md (weights batch with the frame)

lanes.lane: O2 — oracle sweep: fitting and optimizers

findings.title: adam on a ragged MANIFOLD x0 with non-minimal ranks crashes at step 2 with a bare broadcast error
findings.claim: The Adam moment trees m/v are allocated once with corewise_zeros_like(cores) at x0's core shapes. On the ragged MANIFOLD geometry a non-minimal-rank x0 (e.g. d=2 (4,5)/(2,3)/(1,2,1), where n_1=3 > r_1*r_2=2, or d=3 (2,3,2)/(1,2,1,1)) has its redundant rank dropped by the first retraction (the documented caveat), so the second step's corewise_map(m, g) sees mismatched core shapes and raises 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)'. newton_cg, gradient_descent and mc_sgd rebuild everything per step and run fine from the same x0 (ranks drop to minimal); the uniform path reduces x0 transparently via uniform_minimal in _setup, but the ragged _setup branch (t3toolbox/optimizers.py:193-203) does not.
findings.evidence: repro_nonminimal_ragged.py: 'x0 ranks (2, 3) (1, 2, 1) minimal: ((2, 2), (1, 2, 1)) has_minimal_ranks: False / newton_cg OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1) / gradient_descent OK / mc_sgd OK / adam RAISED ValueError operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)'; from the minimal-reduced x0 (same tensor) adam runs. sweep_misc.out 'x0 variants' shows the d=3 analogue: 'EXC nonminimal ragged adam: ValueError ... (3,5) (2,5)' while 'OK nonminimal uniform adam'.
findings.repro_output:
newton_cg OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
gradient_descent OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
mc_sgd OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
adam RAISED ValueError operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)
reduced x0 ranks (2, 2) (1, 2, 1) same tensor: True
newton_cg from minimal x0 OK
findings.proposed_fix: Reduce a ragged x0 to minimal ranks in the ragged branch of optimizers._setup (mirror of uniform_minimal: t3svd + rank_adjustment_sweep('right_to_left')), or in backend adam re-allocate m/v with corewise_zeros_like when the retracted core shapes change; at minimum reject a non-minimal ragged x0 with a clear message.
findings.supported_path: topt.adam(t3m.MANIFOLD, 'apply', ww, b, x0, rng, batch) with any TuckerTensorTrain x0 whose ranks are not minimal (e.g. TuckerTensorTrain.randn((4,5),(2,3),(1,2,1))); the docstring says 'x0: initial point (any cores; the geometry orthogonalizes internally)' and docs/fitting_and_optimization.md claims 4 optimizers x 2 geometries.
findings.related_known: Retract's non-minimal-frame 'caveat' (docs/numerical_contracts.md:120) is the mechanism; the uniform-only minimal reduction is documented at backend/uniform_fitting.py:351 ('The ragged layer tolerates non-minimal ranks').

findings.title: adam on MANIFOLD is gauge-dependent: numpy-eager, jax-eager, jit, ragged and uniform give different iterates
findings.claim: Adam accumulates m/v in the coordinates of the current orthonormal frame, which on MANIFOLD is re-chosen every step by an SVD whose sign/gauge convention differs between numpy and jax and between the ragged and uniform orthogonalizations; nothing transports the moments, so the iterate is not a function of the point. The same adam call therefore returns results differing at the 3e-3..4e-2 level between numpy-eager and jax-eager (no jit involved), eager and jit, and ragged and uniform, while adam on COREWISE and every other optimizer on MANIFOLD agree to ~1e-15. This contradicts docs/fitting_and_optimization.md:14 ('4 optimizers x 2 geometries ... no combinatorial code') and :288-290 ('a single kernel runs numpy-eager, jax-eager, or jit-compiled') for this cell; adam's docstrings only say COREWISE is 'intended'.
findings.evidence: repro_adam_manifold_gauge.py (x64, 50 Adam steps, apply, d=3): 'MANIFOLD: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 5.7e-03 | vs jit 6.5e-03 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 6.9e-03 / COREWISE: 2.5e-16 | 4.6e-16 | 1.6e-16 / newton_cg MANIFOLD: eager vs jit 7.2e-15, ragged vs uniform 5.8e-15'. sweep_misc.out: every MANIFOLD and shared-MANIFOLD row (ragged and uniform, all kinds, with/without reg) shows adam eager-vs-jit 2e-3..4e-2 while newton_cg/mc_sgd are <6e-14; all COREWISE rows OK to 1e-15.
findings.repro_output:
MANIFOLD: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 5.7e-03 | vs jit 6.5e-03 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 6.9e-03
COREWISE: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 2.5e-16 | vs jit 4.6e-16 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 1.6e-16
newton_cg MANIFOLD: eager vs jit 7.2e-15, ragged vs uniform 5.8e-15
findings.proposed_fix: Document in adam's backend+frontend docstrings and in docs/fitting_and_optimization.md §2.4/§4.5 that on MANIFOLD the moments are not transported, so results depend on the frame gauge (backend- and layer-dependent) and adam should be used with COREWISE; alternatively warn/raise on a manifold geometry, or transport/reset m and v each step.
findings.supported_path: topt.adam(t3m.MANIFOLD or ut3m.UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, kind, sample, data, x0, rng, batch[, use_jit=True]) — accepted by the signature ('COREWISE (intended) / MANIFOLD (must match x0)').

findings.title: GaussNewtonModel.jacobian return comment and residual field comment omit the uniform PACKED layout
findings.claim: The jacobian return shape comment says 'probe: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,)' and the residual field comment (line 265) says 'len=d, W+C+(Ni,) (probe)', but for a uniform model both are the packed zero-padded ndarray (d,)+W+C+(N,) (and (d,)+(order+1,)+W+C+(N,) for probe_derivatives). Only the sample field comment mentions '(uniform: PACKED)'. A user following the comment (e.g. zipping the jacobian with a ragged residual list) hits a broadcast error — exactly how my driver first failed.
findings.evidence: repro_small_docs.py: 'ragged jacobian (probe): tuple [(12, 4), (12, 5), (12, 6)] / uniform jacobian (probe): ndarray (3, 12, 6) (docstring: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,)) / uniform residual field: ndarray (3, 12, 6)'. The padding is verified zero in sweep_models.py (check packed_pad_zero, 0 failures).
findings.repro_output:
ragged jacobian (probe): tuple [(12, 4), (12, 5), (12, 6)]
uniform jacobian (probe): ndarray (3, 12, 6)  (docstring: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,))
uniform residual field: ndarray (3, 12, 6) (field comment: len=d, W+C+(Ni,) (probe))
findings.proposed_fix: Add the uniform packed form to the jacobian return comment and the residual field comment ('uniform: PACKED (d,)+[(order+1,)]+W+C+(N,), zero-padded'), matching the existing '(uniform: PACKED)' note on sample.
findings.supported_path: fitting.probe_model(ut3m.UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, UniformTuckerTensorTrain, ww, r).jacobian(p)

findings.title: gradient_descent has no use_jit and its docstring does not say so
findings.claim: topt.gradient_descent accepts chunk_size= but no use_jit=; passing use_jit=True is forwarded through **kwargs to the backend and fails with 'TypeError: gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument use_jit'. The module docstring (line 24) correctly scopes use_jit to mc_sgd/adam/newton_cg, but the function docstring never mentions it, so the error is the only cue.
findings.evidence: repro_small_docs.py: gradient_descent(use_jit=True): TypeError gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_jit'
findings.repro_output: gradient_descent(use_jit=True): TypeError gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_jit'
findings.proposed_fix: One-line note in gradient_descent's docstring (eager only; use_jit is on mc_sgd/adam/newton_cg), or accept use_jit and raise a clear ValueError.
findings.related_known: Flagged as a docstring gap in the sampling/optimization map §3 (kwargs check).

lanes.coverage: Built an independent dense oracle (oracle.py; derivative jets via exact polynomial interpolation of S(X; ww+s*pp), no library jet code) and validated it against the library's plain sampling ops (108/108 to <1e-9, d in {1,2,3}, W in {(7,),(3,4)}, orders 1-3). Part 1 (sweep_models.py, 992 cases, 46 s): GaussNewtonModel over {ragged, uniform} x {MANIFOLD, COREWISE, shared(MANIFOLD), shared(COREWISE)} x 6 kinds x orders {1,2,3} x weight {none, per-order, per-mode, (d,order+1) matrix} x {no reg, IdentityRegularizer(0.3)} x W {(12,),(3,4)} x d {3,2}; per case checked objective == 1/2||w.(S(x)-y)||^2 + rho(x) by hand, jacobian(p) == S_lin(dense(Pi p)), gn_quadratic == ||w.Jp||^2 + lambda||Pi p||^2, <q,Hp> == <wJq,wJp> + lambda<Pi q,Pi p>, the weighted adjoint identity <g,v> == <wr, wJv> + reg pairing, FD of the hand objective along retract(tv), and ragged == uniform (objective, |g|, dense(g), gn_quadratic(g)) at the same point: all exact checks pass at 1e-8; the 12 FD misses (1-4e-6, d=2 MANIFOLD) were shown to be h^2 FD truncation (fd_convergence.py). Part 2 (sweep_optimizers.py, 352 cases): newton_cg (callback capturing x_cores: NewtonInfo.objective/misfit/regularization and every history row equal the hand recomputation; obj == misfit + reg), gradient_descent (losses[k] equals hand objective at the k-iteration iterate), mc_sgd and adam (the reported full-batch loss equals the hand objective at the returned point), ragged-vs-uniform trajectories (losses + dense iterates) for newton_cg/gradient_descent: 352/352 pass on minimal-rank starts. Part 3 (sweep_misc.py): jit==eager at x64 for newton_cg/mc_sgd/adam over {ragged,uniform} x {MANIFOLD, COREWISE, shared MANIFOLD} x 4 kind/weight combos x reg (newton/mc_sgd <6e-14; adam MANIFOLD differs -> O2-2); chunk_size None/'auto'/5/1/100 on ragged+uniform, eager+jit (identical to 1e-14); stacked x0 raises NotImplementedError at entry for all four optimizers and both layers (verified before any work by passing a mismatched sample), stacked+regularized model raises; x0 variants random/orthogonalized/zero/non-minimal (O2-1); verbose=True with val data + regularizer on both layers; d=1 ragged all kinds x both geometries; minibatch take invariant S(A; sample_B) == data_B for all 6 kinds, both layers, W=(12,) and (3,4) (check_take.py). Measured the known regularized-Problem.objective-at-raw-x0 item: Problem.objective(raw x0)=84.04 vs hand 245.60, but LocalModel.objective and gradient_descent losses[0] are correct (245.599525) — the optimizer loops only evaluate Problem.objective on retracted left-orthogonal points, so the consequence is confined to direct backend callers; not broader than described.
lanes.not_checked: Custom draw of a non-nominal batch size with a regularizer (documented lambda mis-scaling) and the lambda*batch/n scaling itself (existing test covers); g0norm_newton/g0norm_cg/cg_forcing_power semantics; uniform d=1 (ledger deferral); float32 behaviour under jit; backend make_newton_display with unpacked uniform validation data (HANDOFF backlog); the Armijo accept-after-40-backtracks path (map R3); custom SamplingKind/Geometry/Regularizer subclasses; the scipy/optax bridge examples.

findings.title: entries_ambient_transpose silently returns zero factors for negative indices (siblings wrap)
findings.claim: `t3_entries_ambient_transpose` builds its one-hot CP factors as `xnp.arange(N) == index[i][..., None]`, so any negative index matches nothing and the factor is all zeros. The forward `entries`, the tangent `entries_transpose` (`eye(N)[index]`), and the corewise transpose all wrap negatives numpy-style and agree with the dense tensor, so the ambient transpose alone silently violates its defining adjoint identity `<from_canonical(E^T c), X> == c * entries(X)`. Under jax an out-of-range index makes the forward silently clamp (gather semantics) while the ambient factors are again zero.
findings.evidence: x.entries([-1,-2,-3]) = 8.1457 == xd[-1,-2,-3]; ambient: <from_canonical(E^T c), x>_F = 0.0, expected c*entries = 16.29, ||T|| = 0.0; tangent adjoint -0.45376 == -0.45376; corewise adjoint 22.4056 == 22.4056. jax: x.entries([7,0,0]) -> 2.8671 == xd[6,0,0] (clamped), jax ambient ||T|| = 0.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Build the one-hots with `xnp.eye(N)[index[i]]` (as `_onehot_vectors` already does) so all four entries ops agree, or validate `0 <= index < N` in the frontend `entries*` methods and document that negative indices are unsupported.
findings.supported_path: `TuckerTensorTrain.entries_ambient_transpose(c, index, shape)` with an index the forward `entries` accepts (docstring says only `int`; the numpy forward and the doc's dense check `X.to_dense()[index]` both wrap negatives).

findings.title: Python-float residual crashes tangent/corewise apply+entries transposes in compute_sigma_hat
findings.claim: `compute_sigma_hat` does `c[..., None]` without `xnp.asarray`, so a plain Python float residual (the natural W=C=() case) raises `TypeError: 'float' object is not subscriptable` from `T3Tangent.apply_transpose`, `T3Tangent.entries_transpose`, `x.apply_corewise_transpose` and `x.entries_corewise_transpose`. The ambient twin `apply_ambient_transpose` accepts a bare `1.7` in its own doctest, and the tangent doctests conspicuously write `np.asarray(1.7)`.
findings.evidence: apply_ambient_transpose(1.7, ww): OK; T3Tangent.apply_transpose(1.7, ww, frame): TypeError: 'float' object is not subscriptable; same for entries_transpose, apply_corewise_transpose, entries_corewise_transpose; np.float64 / 0-d ndarray work.
findings.repro_output: T3Tangent.apply_transpose(1.7, ww, frame): TypeError: 'float' object is not subscriptable / x.apply_corewise_transpose(1.7, ww): TypeError: 'float' object is not subscriptable
findings.proposed_fix: `c = xnp.asarray(c)` at the top of `compute_sigma_hat` (or in `_apply_transpose_adjoint`), mirroring `t3_apply_ambient_transpose`.
findings.supported_path: `T3Tangent.apply_transpose(1.7, ww, frame)` / `x.apply_corewise_transpose(1.7, ww)` — the scalar residual of an unstacked apply, written the way the sibling ambient doctest writes it.

findings.title: MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame, t3) and transport crash at d=1 (IndexError in tt_zipper)
findings.claim: `tv_project_t3_onto_tangent_space` calls `tt_zipper_left_to_right(cores[:-1], ...)`, which indexes `coresA[0]` on an empty tuple when d=1, so `MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame, <TuckerTensorTrain>)` and `MANIFOLD.transport` raise `IndexError: tuple index out of range` for one-mode T3s. The dense path `project_ambient(frame, ndarray)` and `MANIFOLD.project` work at d=1, and d=1 T3s are supported everywhere else (tests use `((8,),(4,),(4,5))`). Reached from this lane via the documented 'tangent = projection of ambient back-projection' route.
findings.evidence: MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame_d1, t3): IndexError: tuple index out of range; MANIFOLD.transport at d=1: IndexError; MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame_d1, dense): OK -> (7,); MANIFOLD.project(tangent) at d=1: OK; d=2 t3 path OK.
findings.repro_output: MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame_d1, t3): IndexError: tuple index out of range / MANIFOLD.transport at d=1: IndexError: tuple index out of range / MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame_d1, dense): OK -> (7,)
findings.proposed_fix: Guard the empty-zipper case in `tv_project_t3_onto_tangent_space` (skip the left/right zippers, or have `tt_zipper_*` return `()` for an empty core list) so d=1 works on the T3 path as it does on the dense path.
findings.supported_path: `t3m.MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame, t3.TuckerTensorTrain.from_canonical(...))` or `MANIFOLD.transport(v, frame)` on any d=1 T3.

findings.title: dense_probe crashes at d=1 with a non-empty probe stack W
findings.claim: `dense_probe` (public, in `__all__`, used as the oracle in doctests) builds an einsum whose output subscripts include the `W` letters, but at d=1 no probe vector is contracted for the single free mode, so the `W` letters never appear in an input and numpy raises `ValueError: einstein sum subscripts string included output subscript 'b' which never appeared in an input`. `t3_probe` itself is correct at d=1 with W (returns the broadcast `W+C+(N,)`).
findings.evidence: x1.probe(W=(2,)): OK -> (2, 7); dense_probe(W=(2,), d=1): ValueError ...; dense_probe(W=(), d=1): OK -> (7,). Every d=1/W≠() case in the sweep hit this.
findings.repro_output: dense_probe(W=(2,), d=1): ValueError: einstein sum subscripts string included output subscript 'b' which never appeared in an input
findings.proposed_fix: When mode `ii` has no partner vectors (d=1), `xnp.broadcast_to` the result over `W` (or multiply by a `W`-shaped ones derived from `vectors[0]`) instead of naming `W` in the einsum output.
findings.supported_path: `probing.dense_probe(ww, T)` with `T.ndim == 1` (plus stacks) and `ww[0].shape == W + (N,)`, W non-empty.

findings.title: TuckerTensorTrain.entries wrong-length list index raises AttributeError, not the documented ValueError
findings.claim: The error message is formatted with `index.shape[0]`, but the docstring says `index` may be anything convertible to an int array and its first example passes a list; `x.entries([1, 2])` on a d=3 tensor therefore raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'` instead of the documented `ValueError`.
findings.evidence: x.entries([1,2]): AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'; x.entries(np.array([1,2])): ValueError: Wrong number of indices ...
findings.repro_output: x.entries([1,2]): AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'
findings.proposed_fix: Use `len(index)` in the message (it is already used in the condition).
findings.supported_path: `x.entries([i, j])` with the wrong number of indices, index given as a list (the docstring's own spelling).

findings.title: tv_apply_transpose / T3Tangent.apply_transpose docstrings describe the retired scatter implementation
findings.claim: The docstring says the transpose 'needs only the frame sweep (xi-hat, mu-hat, nu-hat, eta-hat) and a single-term scatter assembly (it skips the adjoint perturbation sweep that tv_probe_transpose runs)'. The code does the opposite on both counts: `tv_precompute_apply_frame_sweep` is the lean `(xis, mus)` only (no nu/eta), and `_apply_transpose_adjoint` runs a reverse `sigma_hat` adjoint sweep (its own docstring: 'replaces the old scatter'). `manifold.py:781` repeats 'frame sweep + a single-term scatter assembly'.
findings.evidence: apply.py:191-192 calls `tv_precompute_apply_frame_sweep` (returns `xis, mus`) then `_apply_transpose_adjoint` -> `compute_sigma_hat(...)` (probing.py:812 'adjoint reverse sweep'); apply.py:357-371 docstring: 'the low-memory, K-aware transpose (replaces the old scatter) ... at the cost of the sigma_hat sweep per transpose'.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword both docstrings to: lean `(xi, mu)` frame sweep + one adjoint-state `sigma_hat` reverse sweep; no nu/eta stored, no scatter.

findings.title: TuckerTensorTrain.probe return shape comment/docstring omit the frame stack C (and use an undefined letter X)
findings.claim: The return contract reads `# zz, len=d, elm_shape=X+W+(Ni,)` (`X` is not a block symbol and the order reads frame-outer), and the docstring at :3497-3498 says each probe has `elm_shape=W+(Ni,)`. The actual output, frame-inner `W + C + (Ni,)`, is printed by the method's own doctest three lines later as `(4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 14)`.
findings.evidence: tucker_tensor_train.py:3483 `elm_shape=X+W+(Ni,)`; :3497 'each with elm_shape=W+(Ni,)'; doctest :3527-3529 prints `(4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 14)` for W=(4,5,1), C=(2,3); sweep asserts `W+C+(Ni,)`.
findings.repro_output: probe[i] checks pass with shape W+C+(Ni,) for all stacks (DONE. failures: 32, all d=1 oracle exceptions)
findings.proposed_fix: Change both to `W+C+(Ni,)`.

findings.title: compute_mu shape comment says left_tt_cores len=d-1; all callers pass d, and d-1 silently truncates
findings.claim: The signature comment `left_tt_cores: len=d-1` contradicts every caller (`t3_probe`, `tv_probe`, both precompute sweeps, `tv_apply`), which pass all d cores (the scan discards the terminal carry). A backend user following the comment gets `len(mus) = d-1`, and the downstream `compute_eta` (a ragged map over `len(xs[0])`) silently returns d-1 etas with no error. This is the designated signature-style reference module.
findings.evidence: len(mus) with d cores: 3, with d-1 cores: 2; compute_eta with the d-1 mus -> len(etas) = 2 (no error).
findings.repro_output: len(mus) with d cores: 3  with d-1 cores: 2 / compute_eta with the d-1 mus -> len(etas) = 2 (silently d-1; no error)
findings.proposed_fix: Change the comment to `len=d` (the output comment `mus. len=d` is already right).

findings.title: transposes.md: corewise transpose is the pullback J^T A, not a projection of the ambient back-projection
findings.claim: The doc states 'corewise = the ambient back-projection projected onto the core-parametrized tangent space at X (the span of single-core perturbations)'. With a dense corewise Jacobian J, the corewise gradient equals `J^T A` exactly, but `J g` differs from the orthogonal projection `J J^+ A` by relative error 18.7 (`||J^T J - I|| = 412`). The neighbouring claim for the tangent transpose (line 39) IS true (verified: `project_ambient(from_canonical(ambient)) == project(J^T)` for all three ops), because that frame is orthonormal and gauged.
findings.evidence: corewise gradient == J^T A: True; J g == orthogonal projection of A onto range(J): False, relerr = 18.717; project_ambient==project(JT) passes for apply/entries/probe at d>=2 in the sweep.
findings.repro_output: corewise gradient == J^T A (pullback): True / J g == orthogonal projection of A onto range(J): False   relerr = 18.717241435758293
findings.proposed_fix: Reword line 37 to 'the ambient back-projection pulled back through the core parametrization (J_cores^T applied to it)'; keep line 39 as is.

findings.title: entries_apply_probe.md §7 names TuckerTensorTrain.{entries,apply}_transpose, which do not exist
findings.claim: The code-pointer section says 'Frontend: `TuckerTensorTrain.{entries,apply,probe}` and `{entries,apply}_transpose` (tucker_tensor_train.py)'. The frontend transpose methods are `{entries,apply,probe}_{ambient,corewise}_transpose` (six methods); no unqualified `apply_transpose`/`entries_transpose` exists on `TuckerTensorTrain` (by design, per transposes.md). Also line 67's dense check `result == X.to_dense()[index]` only works for a single index tuple, not the documented `(d,)+W` array (needs `tuple(index)`).
findings.evidence: grep 'def .*transpose' tucker_tensor_train.py -> probe_ambient_transpose, probe_corewise_transpose, apply_ambient_transpose, entries_ambient_transpose, apply_corewise_transpose, entries_corewise_transpose (+ the *_corewise_derivatives_transpose trio).
findings.proposed_fix: List the six real method names; write the dense check as `X.to_dense()[tuple(index)]`.

findings.title: Minor: dead conditionals, duplicate line, notation drift in the signature-style reference, stale K letter, undocumented jax clamp
findings.claim: (a) `probing.py:258, 453, 826, 942`: `reverse = tt_reverse if is_uniform else tt_reverse` has identical branches (4x). (b) `entries.py:70,74`: `index = xnp.array(index)` twice. (c) Shape-comment notation drift in the reference module: the right bond is `rRi` at `:582, :621, :1125, :1220` vs `rR(i+1)` in the other 28 uses; `compute_sigma` `:393` column misaligned; `dense_probe` docstring lists parameters in the opposite order to its signature (`:1439-1444`); `tv_apply_transpose` `:173` says `c: W + C` though `K` is accepted. (d) `manifold.py:666` '(V = the probe stack)' uses the pre-rename letter for K. (e) Under jax an out-of-range `entries` index silently clamps (forward and tangent) where numpy raises IndexError; undocumented.
findings.evidence: grep output in the lane report; jax: x.entries([7,0,0]) -> 2.8671 == xd[6,0,0] (clamped) while numpy raises IndexError.
findings.repro_output: numpy forward x.entries([7,0,0]): IndexError: index 7 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 7 / jax forward x.entries([7,0,0]): OK -> 2.867105007171631   vs clamped dense xd[6,0,0] = 2.867104981695296
findings.proposed_fix: Collapse the identical branches to `reverse = tt_operations.tt_reverse`; drop the duplicate line; normalize `rRi` -> `rR(i+1)`; fix the `V` letter; add a one-line note that jax clamps out-of-range indices (or validate in the frontend).

findings.title: t3m(method='inplace_fused') ignores max_tt_ranks on the last bond when rd != 1
findings.claim: t3m_inplace_fused (the frontend default method, tucker_tensor_train.py:2032) never squashes the boundary TT bonds, unlike t3svd / t3_inner_product / t3_norm / t3m_form_then_round. With a non-1 right boundary bond on either operand the product's last bond rd = rd_x*rd_y survives untouched and uncapped, so a scalar or per-position max_tt_ranks is silently violated at position d, the output is asymmetric (left bond squashed to 1, right not), and the truncation quality is markedly worse than form_then_round. The class docstring explicitly allows r0,rd != 1 and the t3m docstring promises 'a scalar caps every position' with no tails precondition.
findings.evidence: x tt_ranks=(2,2,2,3), y (3,3,2,2), shape (5,6,7): max_tt=3,max_tk=3 -> form_then_round ranks ((3,3,3),(1,3,3,1)) relerr 3.4e-02; inplace_fused ranks ((3,3,3),(1,3,3,6)) cap NOT honored, relerr 1.2e-01. max_tt=(1,3,3,1) -> inplace_fused (1,3,3,6). Stacked (2,): (1,3,3,6), relerr 3.4e-01 vs 5.4e-02. Under jit squaring a (2,2,2,3) operand with cap 3 reported tt_ranks (1,3,3,9). With tails=1 the same calls honor the cap.
findings.repro_output: max_tt=3,max_tk=3  inplace_fused  ranks ((3, 3, 3), (1, 3, 3, 6))  caps honored tt=False tucker=True  relerr 1.17e-01  |  form_then_round ranks ((3, 3, 3), (1, 3, 3, 1)) caps honored tt=True relerr 3.43e-02
findings.proposed_fix: Apply tt_squash_tails to both operands' TT cores at the top of t3m_inplace_fused (as t3_inner_product does at t3_linalg.py:183-184) so boundary bonds are 1 before the sweep; alternatively squash/cap the final bond after the sweep.
findings.supported_path: x.t3m(y, max_tt_ranks=...) or x.t3m(y, method='inplace_fused', ...) on any TuckerTensorTrain whose boundary TT ranks are not 1 (allowed per the class docstring, e.g. from_tensor_train, resize, or the constructor)
findings.related_known: docs/t3m_methods.md:56 claims 'the boundary bonds stay 1' (see R1-10)

findings.title: t3m(method='swap') crashes or mis-structures the result with non-1 boundary TT bonds
findings.claim: t3m_swap does not squash boundary bonds either. When both operands have rd != 1 it raises a raw einsum broadcast ValueError from _t3m_contract_pair (:456) for every truncation spec. When the non-1 bonds are on the left it runs but produces a wrong rank structure — the boundary bond migrates to the opposite side (inputs rd=1 -> output rd=3) — with much larger error than the other methods.
findings.evidence: both rd!=1 (2 vs 3), r0=1: swap RAISED ValueError 'operands could not be broadcast together with remapped shapes ... (2,2,3)->(2,2,newaxis,newaxis,3) (2,2,2)'. both r0!=1 (2 vs 3), rd=1: swap ranks ((3,3,3),(2,3,3,3)) relerr 6.8e-01 vs form_then_round ((3,3,3),(1,3,3,1)) 1.3e-01. y r0=3 only: swap -> (1,3,3,3). Stacked (2,) identical.
findings.repro_output: both rd!=1 (2 vs 3), r0=1    swap   RAISED ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with remapped shapes [original->remappe  |  both r0!=1 (2 vs 3), rd=1   swap   ranks ((3, 3, 3), (2, 3, 3, 3)) relerr 6.83e-01
findings.proposed_fix: Same as R1-1: tt_squash_tails both operands at the start of t3m_swap (before the down-orthogonalization at :550), and add a tails!=1 case to tests/test_t3m.py for all three methods.
findings.supported_path: x.t3m(y, method='swap', max_tt_ranks=...) on operands with r0 or rd != 1
findings.related_known: docs/t3m_methods.md:56 'boundary bonds stay 1' (R1-10)

findings.title: entries() with a wrong-length list index raises AttributeError instead of ValueError
findings.claim: The length-mismatch ValueError message is built with index.shape[0], but index is documented as 'array or convertible to NDArray' and the doctests pass plain lists; a wrong-length list therefore dies with AttributeError before the intended ValueError is raised.
findings.evidence: x.entries([1,2]) on a d=3 T3 -> AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'; x.entries(np.array([1,2])) -> the intended ValueError.
findings.repro_output: [entries([1,2])] RAISED AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'shape'
findings.proposed_fix: Use str(len(index)) in the message (line 3380).
findings.supported_path: TuckerTensorTrain.entries(list_of_wrong_length)

findings.title: __mul__ with a wrong-shape ndarray uses a bare assert; docstring promises ValueError
findings.claim: assert(other.shape == self.stack_shape + self.shape) is the only shape check on the T3 * ndarray path. It raises a message-less AssertionError (docstring :1974 says ValueError), and under python -O the check disappears and numpy broadcasting takes over. House rule: structural problems must hard-error in all modes.
findings.evidence: x * np.random.randn(5,6) -> 'AssertionError: ' (empty message); stacked xs * randn(5,6,7) -> same.
findings.repro_output: [x * randn(5,6)] RAISED AssertionError:
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the assert with the same ValueError that __add__ raises at :1920-1924.
findings.supported_path: TuckerTensorTrain * ndarray
findings.related_known: map_core_ragged §3 lists the ~28 structural asserts; the __mul__ dead use_jax param is the separate known item

findings.title: __add__ and inner raise NotImplementedError on stack-shape mismatch; docstrings say ValueError
findings.claim: Both docstrings ('Raises ValueError if shapes and/or stack shapes of self and other are inconsistent', :1857 and :2175) disagree with the code, which raises NotImplementedError for a stack_shape mismatch (:1909, :2303).
findings.evidence: x + xs -> NotImplementedError: Cannot add TuckerTensorTrains with different stack shapes; x.inner(xs) -> NotImplementedError: Cannot take inner product ... different stack shapes.
findings.repro_output: [x + xs] RAISED NotImplementedError: Cannot add TuckerTensorTrains with different stack shapes.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise ValueError (a stack-shape mismatch is a structural inconsistency, consistent with t3m's ValueError), or amend the two Raises sections.

findings.title: reverse() docstring claims tt_ranks=(1, r(d-1), ..., r1, 1); code returns (rd, ..., r0)
findings.claim: The Returns text says the reversed train has tt_ranks (1, r(d-1), ..., r1, 1), i.e. boundary bonds forced to 1. The code (tt_reverse) simply reverses the tuple, keeping non-1 boundary bonds; the method's own doctest prints (4, 3, 2, 1) for input (1, 2, 3, 4).
findings.evidence: x with tt_ranks (2,2,3,4): x.reverse().tt_ranks == (4, 3, 2, 2).
findings.repro_output: reverse().tt_ranks = (4, 3, 2, 2)  docstring claims (1, r(d-1),...,r1, 1)
findings.proposed_fix: Change the docstring to tt_ranks=(rd, r(d-1), ..., r1, r0).

findings.title: probe() return shape comment uses an undefined block letter X and drops the frame stack C
findings.claim: The signature comment reads 'zz, len=d, elm_shape=X+W+(Ni,)' (X is not one of the C/W/K blocks) and the prose Returns (:3495-3497) says elm_shape=W+(Ni,), omitting the T3 stack entirely. The actual layout is frame-inner W + C + (Ni,), which the method's own stacked doctest (:3522, shape (4,5,1,2,3,14)) and probe_ambient_transpose's comment (:3557) show.
findings.repro_output: (read; doctest output (4, 5, 1, 2, 3, 14) in the file itself)
findings.proposed_fix: Change the comment to 'elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,)' and the Returns prose to 'elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,) (frame-inner: probe stack W outer, T3 stack C inner)'.

findings.title: Assorted docstring notation errors in the class docstring and the svd/sum/randn method docs

findings.title: TuckerTensorTrain and T3Weights are eq=True dataclasses over array fields: == raises, unhashable
findings.claim: The default dataclass __eq__ compares core tuples elementwise, so x == y on two equal-valued trains raises 'truth value of an array is ambiguous', x != y likewise, and hash(x) is a TypeError; x == x is True only through identity. T3Frame is eq=False. No doc promises equality, but the asymmetry deserves a decision (same at :4644 for T3Weights).

findings.proposed_fix: Either eq=False (identity semantics, hashable, matching T3Frame) or a deliberate value-based __eq__ via corewise comparison; document whichever.

findings.title: compute_orthogonal_representation_ranks wrong on non-minimal input; uniform frame masks built from it make UT3Frame.from_ut3 / UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame non-orthogonal
findings.claim: The function (the map said it had no caller; it is called by backend/ufv_conversions.py:107 to build the uniform frame's prefix masks) computes a right sweep over the ORIGINAL bonds and then derives the left ranks from that, whereas the sweep the library actually runs (fv_conversions.t3_orthogonal_representations) does Tucker down-orth, a LEFT sweep on the original bonds, then a RIGHT sweep over the left-orthogonal chain. On minimal-rank structures both agree, which is why the tests never caught it; on any non-minimal structure the predicted left/right TT ranks are wrong, so the uniform frame masks zero real content / admit phantom rank and the uniform frame is not orthogonal while the ragged frame of the same point is. Under jit/unsafe the manifold projection is silently wrong (29% off); in safe mode the user gets the orthogonality-precondition error for a point they built legitimately. docs/uniform_equivalence_contract.md:33 promises the contract holds on non-minimal input. Optimizer fits are shielded only by uniform_minimal(x0) in optimizers.py:186.
findings.evidence: orth_rep_ranks.py: 185/303 random structures (d 1..4, asymmetric) disagree with T3Frame.from_t3 core shapes; e.g. shape (5,5,5) n (2,2,2) r (1,4,4,1): predicted left (1,2,2,1) right (1,4,2,1), actual left (1,2,4,1) right (1,2,2,1). orth_rep_fix.py: corrected recurrence (left_{i+1}=min(left_i*n_i, r_{i+1}); right_i=min(left_i, n_i*right_{i+1}); down_i=min(up_i, left_i*right_{i+1})) matches 301/301. On that point T3Frame.from_t3 is_orthogonal True (9e-16) but UT3Frame.from_ut3 is_orthogonal False (4e-2); on the minimal_ranks doctest structure (13,14,15,16),(4,5,6,7),(1,4,99,7,1) residual 1.0, right mask rank 42 vs content 20. safe_mode_uniform_frame.py: safe mode UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.project_ambient raises 'requires an orthogonal frame'; unsafe: uniform vs ragged projection rel diff 2.947e-01; control on minimal point 4.97e-16.

findings.proposed_fix: Replace ranks.py:548-573 with the sweep-faithful recurrence (left sweep first on tt_ranks, right sweep over left_ranks, down_i = min(up_i, left_i*right_{i+1})); add a direct test against T3Frame.from_t3 core shapes on random NON-minimal structures and a uniform-frame orthogonality test on a non-minimal point.

findings.title: rank_adjustment_sweep 'compose both directions for guaranteed minimal ranks' is false when a Tucker rank exceeds its mode size (n_i > N_i), ragged unshared and shared
findings.claim: The sweep re-SVDs only the TT core's outer unfolding (t3_down_svd_tt_core) and never the Tucker factor, so the n_i <= N_i ceiling is never applied: a Tucker rank above the mode size is reduced to rL*rR, not to N. The claim is repeated in the frontend rank_adjustment_sweep docstring, docs/t3svd_minimal_ranks.md and docs/contributor/t3svd_design_rationale.md. Such inputs are legal (the minimal_ranks doctest builds one). Lossless, so a doc/contract mismatch rather than a wrong tensor. With n_i <= N_i the composed sweeps do reach the minimal ranks (150/150 unshared, 150/150 shared).

findings.title: Documented truncation rule 'sigma < max(atol, rtol*sigma1)' / parsimony bound 'r_hat <= #{sigma >= tau}' contradicts the code's tail-Frobenius-energy rule
findings.claim: linalg.truncated_svd's signature comments and Parameters (lines 81-82, 102, 105) say singular values with sigma < max(atol, rtol*sigma1) are removed; docs/contributor/t3svd_verification.md's Claim, its proof ('The routine chooses r_k = #{ j : sigma_j >= tau_k }') and Algorithm 2, and the TuckerTensorTrain.t3svd doctest comment ('parsimony: each chosen rank <= #{ original singular values >= tau }') all state the per-singular-value rule. The code (linalg.py:201-205) keeps K = #{ j : ||sigma[j:]||_2 >= max(rtol*||A||_F, atol) } (tail energy, relative to the Frobenius norm, not sigma1), which keeps at least as many and can keep far more, so the documented bound is violated on flat-tailed spectra. The tail-energy rule is the intended one (it is what makes the sqrt(2d-1)*tol accumulated-error bound hold) and the actual tests (test_tucker_tensor_train.py:2587-2590, 2929-2933) use it; only the docs, comments and the doctest comment are stale (the doctest passes by luck of the graded spectrum).
findings.evidence: tol_parsimony.py: spectrum [1, 0.05 x20], rtol=0.08: truncated_svd keeps 19; per-sigma rule (either sigma1- or ||A||_F-relative) would keep 1. t3svd(rtol=0.1) on a flat-tailed tensor: chosen Tucker ranks (6,7,6) vs the doc's bound rho = (1,6,6); 'claim r_hat <= rho holds? False'.
findings.repro_output: (a) truncated_svd(rtol=0.08) on spectrum [1, 0.05 x20]: kept rank = 19 ; per-sigma rule would keep 1 ; code rule #{j : ||s[j:]|| >= tol} = 19 ; (a2) t3svd(rtol=0.1): chosen tucker ranks (6, 7, 6) ; doc parsimony bound rho = (1, 6, 6) ; claim r_hat <= rho holds? False
findings.proposed_fix: Restate the rule as tail energy ('drop the trailing singular values whose tail 2-norm falls below max(rtol*||A||_F, atol)') in linalg.py, rewrite the verification note's Claim/Algorithm 2 as r_hat <= #{ j : ||sigma_{j:}|| >= tau } (the projection lemma still proves it since tails contract), and fix the t3svd doctest comment.

findings.title: t3m_swap silently wrong when both inputs have equal boundary TT ranks != 1 (crashes when they differ)
findings.claim: t3m_swap builds the 2d-chain Gx_o + reversed(Gy_o) and merges the seam pair (d-1, d) with _t3m_contract_pair, whose einsum '...anb,...bmc->...anmc' contracts Gx's trailing bond rd_x against Gy's trailing bond rd_y. The represented-tensor semantics (to_dense, t3_mult, t3_inner_product) sum each boundary bond with a ones vector separately, so with rd_x == rd_y != 1 the method returns a wrong Hadamard product with no error, and with rd_x != rd_y it raises a numpy broadcast ValueError from inside einsum. TuckerTensorTrain.validate permits r0, rd != 1 (class docstring: 'You can make r0=rd=1 using squash_tails') and t3m only checks shape/stack_shape. form_then_round and inplace_fused are correct on the same inputs. tests/test_t3m.py only uses tt_ranks starting and ending in 1.
findings.evidence: A=randn((4,5,6),(2,3,2),(2,3,2,2)), B=randn(...,(2,2,3,2)): swap max-rank and rtol both give relerr 4.95e-01 vs A.to_dense()*B.to_dense(); form_then_round 2.2e-15, inplace_fused 1.5e-15. With rd 2 vs 3: swap raises 'operands could not be broadcast together'. Via the documented segment API: a=A.segment(1,3), b=B.segment(1,3) (tt_ranks (2,2,2)): swap relerr 6.47e-01, others ~6e-16.

findings.title: t3m_swap silently ignores per-position max_tt_ranks given as a numpy array
findings.claim: need_cleanup tests isinstance(max_tt_ranks, typ.Sequence); a numpy array is not a typ.Sequence, so the final t3svd cleanup -- which the docstring says is the only mechanism that honors per-position bonds in the swap method -- is skipped, while ranks.normalize_max_ranks accepts the array without complaint. The per-position caps are silently exceeded; inplace_fused honors the same array.
findings.evidence: A.t3m(B, method='swap', max_tt_ranks=[1,2,3,2,1]) -> tt_ranks (1,2,3,2,1); A.t3m(B, method='swap', max_tt_ranks=np.array([1,2,3,2,1])) -> tt_ranks (1,3,3,3,1); A.t3m(B, method='inplace_fused', max_tt_ranks=np.array(...)) -> (1,2,3,2,1).
findings.repro_output:
swap max_tt_ranks list  -> tt_ranks (1, 2, 3, 2, 1)
swap max_tt_ranks array -> tt_ranks (1, 3, 3, 3, 1) (cap was [1, 2, 3, 2, 1])
fused max_tt_ranks array -> tt_ranks (1, 2, 3, 2, 1)
findings.proposed_fix: Decide need_cleanup with np.ndim(max_tt_ranks) > 0 (or max_tt_ranks is not None and not isinstance(max_tt_ranks, (int, np.integer))) so arrays and sequences are treated alike.
findings.supported_path: TuckerTensorTrain.t3m(other, method='swap', max_tt_ranks=np.array([...])) -- the signature says Sequence[int], but normalize_max_ranks accepts an array and the other two methods honor it.

findings.title: linalg.truncated_svd (and all directional/pair wrappers) document a per-singular-value rtol/atol rule; code implements a tail-Frobenius rule
findings.claim: The signature comments (lines 81-82) and the Parameters section (101-106) say rtol/atol 'remove singular values satisfying sigma < maximum(atol, rtol*sigma1)'. The code (200-205) keeps K = #{i : ||sigma[i:]||_2 >= max(rtol*||A||_F, atol)} -- a tail-Frobenius-energy rule relative to ||A||_F, not a per-sigma rule relative to sigma1. The identical comment is copied into left_svd, right_svd, up_svd and the four *_svd_pair (222-223, 265-266, 304-305, 345-346, 391-392, 434-435, 483-484). The frontend t3svd docstrings say 'relative tolerance (in Frobenius norm)', which matches the code, so the mismatch is confined to linalg.py. The Parameters block also lists min_rank twice (line 99 should be max_rank).
findings.evidence: sigma=(1,.08,.08,.08,.08), rtol=0.1: doc rule keeps 1, code keeps 4 (tail norms [1.0127 0.16 0.1386 0.1131 0.08] vs 0.1013). sigma=(1,.3,.3), atol=0.35: doc rule keeps 1, code keeps 2. left_svd with rtol=0.1 keeps 4 too.
findings.repro_output:
rtol=0.1: doc criterion (sigma < rtol*sigma1) would keep 1 ; code keeps 4
sigma = [1.  0.3 0.3] atol=0.35: doc criterion would keep 1 ; code keeps 2
findings.proposed_fix: Rewrite the comment and Parameters text in truncated_svd and the eight wrappers to the implemented rule: drop the trailing singular values whose combined Frobenius norm is below max(atol, rtol*||A||_F); fix the duplicated min_rank entry.
findings.supported_path: linalg.truncated_svd(A, rtol=...) and every t3 SVD step that forwards rtol/atol.

findings.title: t3_norm(use_orthogonalization=False) still orthogonalizes (twice); frontend norm docstring promises zippering without orthogonalization
findings.claim: The use_orthogonalization=False branch of t3_norm calls t3_inner_product(x, x) without forwarding the flag, so t3_inner_product's default True runs t3_left_orthogonalize on both operands -- two orthogonalizations versus one for True. TuckerTensorTrain.norm's docstring (tucker_tensor_train.py:2378-2381) says False means 'compute norm with conventional zippering (faster, more suited for automatic differentiation)'. The numerical value is correct; the parameter is not honored.
findings.evidence: Counting calls to t3_left_orthogonalize: t3_norm(True) -> 1 call; t3_norm(False) -> 2 calls; x.norm(use_orthogonalization=False) -> 2 calls; t3_inner_product(use_orthogonalization=False) -> 0 calls. Values identical to the dense norm.
findings.repro_output:
t3_norm(use_orthogonalization=True): t3_left_orthogonalize called 1 time(s)
t3_norm(use_orthogonalization=False): t3_left_orthogonalize called 2 time(s)
frontend x.norm(use_orthogonalization=False): called 2 time(s)
findings.proposed_fix: norm_sq = t3_inner_product(x, x, use_orthogonalization=False) in the else branch.
findings.supported_path: TuckerTensorTrain.norm(use_orthogonalization=False) / t3_norm(x, use_orthogonalization=False).

findings.title: stacking.stack (TuckerTensorTrain.stack, T3Frame.stack, T3Tangent.stack_*) raises ConcretizationTypeError under jit
findings.claim: stack moves the leading stack axes with xnp.moveaxis(stacked, source=xnp.arange(len(axes)), destination=axes). On the jax path xnp.arange is a traced array inside jit, and jnp.moveaxis requires concrete axis indices, so any stack inside a jitted function fails; eager jax works and unstack works under jit. test_dispatch never jits a stack.
findings.evidence: jax.jit(lambda u, v: TuckerTensorTrain.stack((u, v)).data)(x, y) -> ConcretizationTypeError: Abstract tracer value encountered where concrete value is expected: traced array with shape int32[1]; same for stacking.stack with axes=() and (0,); eager stack returns stack_shape (2,); jitted unstack returns 2 leaves.
findings.repro_output:
eager TuckerTensorTrain.stack((x, y)) -> (2,)
jit   TuckerTensorTrain.stack((x, y)) -> ConcretizationTypeError: Abstract tracer value encountered where concrete value is expected: traced array with shape int32[1]
jit   stacking.unstack axes=(0,) -> 2
findings.proposed_fix: Use a Python tuple for the axis list: xnp.moveaxis(stacked, source=tuple(range(len(axes))), destination=tuple(axes)); add a jitted stack to test_dispatch.
findings.supported_path: jax.jit over a function that calls TuckerTensorTrain.stack / T3Frame.stack / T3Tangent.stack_tangents / stack_frame (registered pytrees per docs/batching_and_stacking.md §7).

findings.title: Structural checks via assert: empty-message AssertionError normally, silent wrong result or obscure error under python -O (TuckerTensorTrain.__mul__ documents ValueError)
findings.claim: __mul__'s NDArray branch guards other.shape == stack_shape + shape with a bare assert while its docstring says 'Raises ValueError if shapes and/or stack shapes ... are inconsistent'. Normally the user gets an AssertionError with no message; under python -O the assert is stripped and a wrong-shaped array is silently broadcast into to_dense()*other. The same pattern (house rule: structural problems must hard-error always) is used in t3_linalg.t3_add:61, t3_inner_product:195, t3_mult:258 (stack-shape mismatch), t3_operations.t3_sum:296-297 and t3_linalg.t3_sum_stack:117 (axis range), and common.xcat/xappend/xprepend:346-396, which degrade to empty AssertionErrors normally and to numpy broadcast/IndexError messages under -O.
findings.evidence: python: x*np.ones((1,5)) on a (4,5) T3 -> AssertionError (empty message). python -O: x*np.ones((1,5)) -> returned (4,5) array; x*np.ones(5) -> returned (4,5); t3_add stack (2,)+(3,) -> ValueError 'all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match'; t3_sum axis=5 -> IndexError; t3_inner_product stack mismatch -> einsum broadcast ValueError.
findings.repro_output:
[-O] __mul__ by array of shape (1,5) (doc: must equal stack_shape+shape) -> returned (4, 5)
[-O] x * ones(5) (broadcast-compatible wrong shape) -> returned (4, 5)
[normal] -> AssertionError: (empty message)
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the structural asserts with explicit raise ValueError(...) carrying the offending shapes (at minimum __mul__, t3_add, t3_inner_product, t3_mult, t3_sum, t3_sum_stack, xcat/xappend/xprepend).
findings.supported_path: x * ndarray with a wrong but broadcast-compatible shape (documented as 'requires other.shape = stack_shape + shape'), under python -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE.

findings.title: ValueHashedFields/ValueHashedMasks hash-eq edge cases: jax-array field unhashable, dtype-only mask difference breaks hash/eq contract, mask-count mismatch compares equal
findings.claim: ValueHashedFields._value_key only value-keys np.ndarray; a jax array field falls through to 'return v', so hash() raises TypeError (unhashable ArrayImpl) and == raises 'truth value of an array is ambiguous' -- the docstring says arrays are compared by content without saying numpy-only. ValueHashedMasks hashes (shape, dtype, bytes) but compares with np.array_equal, so a bool mask and an int8 mask with equal values are == but hash differently; __eq__ zips .data so holders with different numbers of masks compare equal. Also F(nan) != F(nan) except by identity, and -0.0 vs 0.0 arrays are unequal. None is reachable from the documented API today (masks are bool by construction; SamplingKind.weight is canonicalized in __post_init__), but the mixin is the jit cache key.
findings.evidence: Masks bool vs int8: eq True, hash equal False; different number of masks: eq True; Fields jax field: hash -> TypeError unhashable; eq -> ValueError ambiguous; Fields NaN float: self == copy -> False.
findings.repro_output:
Masks: bool vs int8 same values: eq -> True
Masks: bool vs int8 same values: hash equal -> False
Masks: different number of masks (zip truncates): eq -> True
Fields: jax array field: hash -> TypeError: unhashable type: 'jaxlib._jax.ArrayImpl'
findings.proposed_fix: In _value_key treat any is_ndarray leaf via np.asarray (or raise a clear TypeError for jax arrays); in ValueHashedMasks.__eq__ compare lengths and dtype or hash on np.asarray(m, bool).

findings.title: tree_contains_jax / tree_to_jax / stacking.tree_depth recurse forever on a str leaf
findings.claim: These helpers recurse on isinstance(T, typ.Sequence); a str is a Sequence whose [0] is itself a str, so a string anywhere in a tree gives RecursionError (tree_contains_jax, tree_depth) or, in tree_to_jax, type(T)(generator) which turns the leaf into the repr of a generator object. No library call site puts strings in data trees, so this is only a robustness gap for raw-.data users.
findings.evidence: tree_contains_jax((np.ones(2), 'left')) -> RecursionError; tree_depth('ab') -> RecursionError; tree_to_jax((np.ones(2), 'ab')) -> (Array([1., 1.]), '<generator object tree_to_jax.<locals>.<genexpr> ...>').
findings.repro_output:
tree_contains_jax((np.ones(2), "left")) -> RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded in comparison
tree_to_jax((np.ones(2), "ab")) -> (Array([1., 1.], dtype=float32), '<generator object ...>')
findings.proposed_fix: Exclude str/bytes from the Sequence test (isinstance(T, (tuple, list))) in the three helpers.

findings.title: t3_right_orthogonalize and the single-core SVD / relative-to orthogonalization steps are correct but have no test
findings.claim: The map flagged t3_right_orthogonalize (no caller, no test) as possibly dead or wrong. Verified: it preserves the represented tensor and yields right-orthogonal form (t3_orthogonality_residual(side='right') ~1e-15) on 4 structures x 3 stack shapes including unsquashed tails -- the exact mirror of t3_left_orthogonalize's contract. Same sweep passes for t3_orthogonalize_relative_to_{tucker,tt}_core (every ii; all other cores orthogonal in the expected direction, the ii-th TT core up-orthonormal), t3_{down_svd_tucker,left_svd_tt,right_svd_tt,down_svd_tt,up_svd_tt}_core (every ii incl. the boundary branches) and t3_up_orthogonalize_tt_cores. None has a direct test reference in tests/.
findings.evidence: right_orth shape=(4,5,6,3) stack=(2,3): dense relerr=1.1e-15, right-res=1.1e-15 (left-res=6.2e+04); FAILURES: none over the full sweep.
findings.repro_output:
right_orth  shape=(4, 5, 6, 3)   stack=(2, 3) dense relerr=1.1e-15 right-res=1.1e-15 (left-res=6.2e+04)
FAILURES: none

findings.title: Copy-paste errors in linalg.py / t3_orthogonalization.py / t3_operations.py / stacking.py signature comments and docstrings
findings.claim: left_svd_pair and right_svd_pair return comment 'new_G1 shape=(..., r, nb, nj)' should read nk (lines 349, 395). The rank-bound comment 'minimum(ni*na, nj)' was copied into right_svd (should be min(ni, na*nj); 263-264), up_svd and up_svd_pair (min(ni*nj, na); 302-303, 432-433), down_svd_pair (min(na, N); 481-482). right_svd/up_svd shape comments omit the leading '...' stack both support (verified on stacks). t3_operations.py:184 tucker_change_core_shapes docstring says 'for TT cores'. t3_orthogonalization.py:347 t3_up_svd_tt_core says 'right unfolding' (it is the up unfolding); :294 has a duplicated assignment; :250 names a local U_i_a_x whose axes are (a,i,x); :225 t3_left_svd_tt_core does not document its ii==d-1 branch (sums the trailing bond with ones). stacking.py:488 basic_uniform_stack says 'into single ragged array tuple'.

findings.title: jax-absent: NameError surfaces through the constructors and tree_to_jax, and to_jax silently returns numpy
findings.claim: With jax uninstalled, get_backend(*, use_jax=True) raises a bare NameError (known). The same NameError is what the user-facing constructors raise -- TuckerTensorTrain.randn/zeros(use_jax=True), t3_corewise_randn(use_jax=True), common.randn(use_jax=True) -- and tree_to_jax, while common.to_jax silently returns a numpy array (it is defined as np.array when jax is absent). Broader than the HANDOFF entry, which names only get_backend.
findings.evidence: jax import blocked: get_backend(False, True), TuckerTensorTrain.randn(use_jax=True), TuckerTensorTrain.zeros(use_jax=True), common.randn(3, use_jax=True), tree_to_jax -> NameError: name 'jnp' is not defined; common.to_jax(np.ones(2)) -> ndarray.

TuckerTensorTrain.randn(use_jax=True) -> NameError: name 'jnp' is not defined
common.to_jax(np.ones(2)) (silent numpy) -> ndarray

findings.title: stacking helpers on malformed trees: tree_zip truncates, stack ignores extra leaves, unstack negative axes use the first leaf's ndim, empty tuples IndexError
findings.claim: tree_zip zips with zip() so unequal lengths are silently truncated; stack derives the structure from T[0]...[0] only, so extra leaves in other elements are silently dropped; unstack normalizes negative axes against the first array leaf's ndim and applies the same absolute axis to every leaf, so on leaves of different ndim a negative axis slices the wrong axis of the other leaves; tree_depth(()) / get_first_leaf(()) raise IndexError; apply_func_to_leaf_subtrees on a non-matching leaf fails with "'int' object is not iterable". All on inputs outside the documented happy path.
findings.evidence: tree_zip((1,2,3),(4,5)) -> ((1,4),(2,5)); stack with an extra leaf in the second element -> [(2,2,3),(2,)]; unstack A(4,2,3),B(2,3) axes=(-2,) -> B leaves of shape (2,) (sliced along its axis 1); tree_depth(()) -> IndexError.
findings.repro_output:
tree_zip((1,2,3),(4,5)) truncates -> ((1, 4), (2, 5))
stack with extra leaf in second element -> [(2, 2, 3), (2,)]
unstack negative axis, leaves of different ndim: A(4,2,3), B(2,3) -> [(4, 3), (2,)]
findings.proposed_fix: Add length checks to tree_zip and a trees_have_same_structure check in stack against the template; document that unstack axes are absolute (or normalize per leaf).

findings.title: Minor backend ergonomics: t3_inner_product list/tuple family concat, t3_sum with ndarray axis, truncated_svd min_rank/max_rank corners
findings.claim: t3_inner_product infers jax-ness with x[0] + x[1] + y[0] + y[1], which raises TypeError when a raw-.data user mixes a list family with a tuple family (every other op uses tree_contains_jax). t3_operations.t3_sum(axis=np.array([...])) fails with 'truth value ambiguous' because an ndarray is not a typ.Sequence. linalg.truncated_svd: a zero matrix with rtol keeps full rank (tol=0); min_rank greater than min(N,M) silently returns fewer; min_rank > max_rank lets min_rank win although the comment states min_rank <= max_rank is required and nothing checks it. common.load_core_families drops a trailing empty family (unreachable: every family has d >= 1 cores).
findings.evidence: t3_inner_product((list(x[0]), x[1]), x) -> TypeError can only concatenate list (not 'tuple') to list; t3_sum(x, axis=np.array([0,1])) -> ValueError truth value ambiguous; truncated_svd(zeros(3,4), rtol=1e-3) kept rank (3,); min_rank=6 on 3x4 -> 3; min_rank=3,max_rank=1 -> 3.
findings.repro_output:
t3_inner_product with list+tuple mixed families: TypeError can only concatenate list (not "tuple") to list
truncated_svd min_rank=3 > max_rank=1 kept rank: (3,) (min_rank wins)
findings.proposed_fix: Use tree_contains_jax((x, y)) in t3_inner_product; accept array-likes via np.atleast_1d in t3_sum axis handling; either validate 1 <= min_rank <= max_rank <= min(N,M) in truncated_svd or document the actual precedence.

findings.title: check_fv_pair accepts a d-mismatched (frame, variations) pair; downstream ops return silent partial results or opaque errors
findings.claim: check_fv_pair compares hole shapes with zip(xVV, yVV) / zip(xHH, yHH) and never compares the number of cores, so a frame with d=3 paired with variations with d=2 (whose two cores fit holes 0 and 1) passes, T3Tangent constructs (validate relies on check_fv_pair), and to_dense / corewise_norm / MANIFOLD.project / MANIFOLD.norm return values (the sum of only the first two modes' terms) with no error, while to_t3, apply and MANIFOLD.retract fail deep inside numpy with unrelated-looking messages. The house rule is that structural problems always raise.

The d=4 variations case also passes and then IndexErrors in to_dense.

check_fv_pair(frame d=3, variations d=2) -> None
T3Tangent constructed: T3Tangent(shape=(5, 6, 7), ...)
  to_dense().shape -> (5, 6, 7)
  corewise_norm() -> 6.989740554290506
  MANIFOLD.norm(t) -> 5.362061795480749
  to_t3() -> ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly...
  apply(ww) -> IndexError: tuple index out of range
  MANIFOLD.retract(t) -> ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,4,1) (2,2,3)
findings.proposed_fix: Add `if variations.d != frame.d: raise ValueError('Inconsistent (T3Frame, T3Variations) pair: frame has d=.. cores, variations have d=..')` before the hole loops (mirroring fv_weights_consistent, which does compare lengths).

findings.title: safety.set_default_safety docstring promises a 'script-level default'; it is per-context (threads see the module default, scoped blocks discard it, cannot select unsafe)
findings.claim: set_default_safety does _safety.set(...) on a ContextVar. The docstring says 'use this for a script-level default'. The function has no test.

after set_default_safety inside safe() block exits: SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=1e-12, rtol_jax=0.001) (the 1e-7 was discarded)

In code the summed path is a jax.lax.scan (:1922, not lax.map) and the kept path _wchunked_concat (:1931-1938) is a Python list comprehension + concatenate — unrolled under jit, no scan — so all chunk intermediates stay co-resident and the peak does not drop on the kept path.

findings.title: Summed chunk path is memory-inert when W // chunk_size == 2 (incl. the default chunk_size=100 for W in [200,299])
findings.claim: _wchunked_sum computes chunk 0 eagerly and scans over jnp.arange(1, n_full). When n_full == 2 the scan has trip count 1; XLA simplifies the single-trip loop away, so chunk 0, chunk 1 and the remainder are co-resident and the peak stays at the dense level. The docstring at :1958 ("Peak ~ chunk_size * (per-W-row) instead of W * (per-W-row)") and docs/chunking.md:29-30 do not hold in that regime; with the default chunk_size=100 this is every W in [200, 299], and a user choosing chunk_size = W/2 to halve memory silently gets no reduction. Numbers are exact regardless.
findings.evidence: memory_analysis temp on assemble_tt_variation_jets (d=4, r=24, order=3, K=1, x64, sum_over_probes=True): W=200 dense 42.8 MiB; cs=100 (n_full=2): 39.6 MiB (expected ~21.4); cs=75 (n_full=2, rem=50): 36.9 (expected ~16.0); cs=50 (n_full=4): 10.8 (as expected). W=300 dense 64.6 MiB; cs=100 (n_full=3): 21.5, cs=75: 16.2, cs=50: 10.8 — all as expected. W=256: cs=128 53.1 MB vs dense 57.4; cs=85 (n_full=3) 21.0; cs=64 14.5.
findings.repro_output:
W=200: dense 42.8 MiB; {100: '39.6 MiB (n_full=2, rem=0, expected ~21.4)', 75: '36.9 MiB (n_full=2, rem=50, expected ~16.0)', 50: '10.8 MiB (n_full=4, rem=0, expected ~10.7)'}
W=300: dense 64.6 MiB; {100: '21.5 MiB (n_full=3, rem=0, expected ~21.5)', 75: '16.2 MiB (n_full=4, rem=0, expected ~16.1)', 50: '10.8 MiB (n_full=6, rem=0, expected ~10.8)'}
findings.proposed_fix: Seed the accumulator with zeros of the chunk output shape (jax.eval_shape(chunk_fn, chunk0, extra)) and scan over jnp.arange(0, n_full), so the loop's trip count is n_full >= 2 whenever chunking engages (optionally fold the remainder into the loop with a padded last chunk); or document the regime.

findings.claim: ManifoldGeometryOps.point_norm_sq reads ‖last TT core‖², exact only for a left-orthogonal input, so a direct backend Problem.objective(x) at a raw (non-left-orthogonal) ragged MANIFOLD point returns a wrong regularized objective. Scope is narrow: COREWISE is exact for any cores, the uniform twin orthogonalizes first, LocalModel.objective and the frontend GaussNewtonModel.objective_value go through the frame, and all four optimizers are unaffected because their iteration-0 values come from the LocalModel and every later Problem.objective call is at a retraction output, which is left-orthogonal to ~1e-15 for both the unshared tv_retract and the shared grouped-t3svd retraction. Armijo comparisons are therefore consistent and no stats row is wrong.
findings.evidence: Raw randn x0 (left-orth residual 34.8): Problem.objective = 1998.03 vs truth 3398.41 (reg term used 3.13 = ½λ‖last core‖² vs true ½λ‖X‖²_HS = 1403.5). COREWISE 2015.62 == truth; uniform 3398.41 == truth; LocalModel.objective 3398.41 == truth; retract outputs left-orth residual 1.8e-15 (unshared) / 8.9e-16 (shared) and Problem.objective correct there; newton_cg history[0].objective and gradient_descent losses[0] == truth.

findings.title: `batch` is NOT ignored when `draw` is given: regularizer λ scales by the nominal batch, not the draw's size
findings.claim: _minibatch_step_problem scales the regularizer by min(batch,n)/n using the nominal `batch` argument regardless of what a custom `draw` returns. The signature comments at backend/optimizers.py:415,459 and t3toolbox/optimizers.py:243,267 say batch is 'ignored if draw given', and docs/fitting_and_optimization.md:405-406 says λ 'keeps the same meaning whatever batch size you use — you do not rescale λ by hand'. Both are false for a custom draw whose size differs from `batch` when a regularizer is attached: the effective λ is silently off by batch/draw_size.
findings.evidence: n=100, custom draw of size 5: batch=5 -> factor 0.050 (consistent); batch=50 -> factor 0.500; batch=100 -> 1.000 (draw-consistent factor is 0.050). mc_sgd with the same draw and rng seed returns different results for batch=5 vs batch=50 (rel diff 0.876) when regularized, identical (0.0) when unregularized.
findings.repro_output: batch= 50 custom draw size=5: regularizer factor used = 0.500 (draw-consistent factor = 0.050) | mc_sgd with draw=my_draw: result differs between batch=5 and batch=50 (same rng seed): rel diff = 8.763e-01 | unregularized: rel diff = 0.000e+00
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the factor from the drawn minibatch inside the step (kind.n_measurements(sample_B)/n — shape-derived, static under jit), or correct the four 'ignored if draw given' comments and §4.9 to say the nominal `batch` governs λ scaling with a custom draw.
findings.supported_path: optimizers.mc_sgd/adam(..., batch, draw=my_draw, regularizer=IdentityRegularizer(λ)) — §2.3 documents custom draws, §4.9 documents the auto-scaling

findings.title: 'An untied initial guess is a non-event for the optimizers' — the backend geometries the optimizers use do not tie at frame, and the corewise backend retract ties differently from the frontend
findings.claim: The optimizers map a SharedGeometry to the backend ManifoldGeometryOps/CorewiseGeometryOps.with_sharing, whose frame() does NOT tie (the base point of the backend frame at an untied x is untied); the untied x0 is tied by the first retraction instead. On the COREWISE backend that retraction aliases group member 0 (result U[0]+mean(V) at every group mode, via t3_alias_tied_tucker_factors), whereas the frontend SharedGeometry.retract ties the sum by the mean (mean(U)+mean(V)), so the two twins disagree on an untied base. On a tied base all four SharedGeometry.retract branches are bit-identical with the backend twins.
findings.evidence: backend ManifoldGeometryOps.frame(untied).base_point tied: False; CorewiseGeometryOps: False. topt.newton_cg(shared_*, untied x0) runs without error and the iterate is tied after step 1. Corewise shared retract on an untied base: backend U[0] is U[1]: True, equals x.U[0]+mean(V): True, equals mean(x.U)+mean(V): False; frontend equals mean(x.U)+mean(V): True; frontend-vs-backend dense rel diff 1.33. Tied base: ragged MANIFOLD/COREWISE max abs core diff 0.0; UNIFORM_MANIFOLD/COREWISE dense rel diff 0.0.
findings.repro_output: backend CorewiseGeometryOps.frame(untied).base_point tied: False | corewise shared retract on an UNTIED base point: backend result U[0] is U[1]: True ; equals x.U[0]+mean(V): True ; equals mean(x.U)+mean(V): False | frontend result U[0] equals mean(x.U)+mean(V): True | frontend vs backend dense rel diff: 1.33e+00
findings.proposed_fix: Tie in the backend frame() when groups is non-empty (t3_tie_tucker_factors / ut3 twin — a bitwise no-op on tied input), which makes the twins agree and the docstring true; or soften the docstring to 'for the frontend model path' and have the backend corewise retract tie by the mean like the frontend.

findings.title: Backend probe kinds silently truncate a per-mode weight whose mode dimension exceeds d
findings.claim: _weight_matrix validates only the order dimension and delegates the mode dimension to the frontend (:212-213); _make_weight's apply_w indexes wp[i] for i < d, so a raw-.data user building probe_kind / probe_derivatives_kind with a weight of m > d rows gets a kind that constructs fine and silently applies only the first d rows (m < d raises an IndexError only at sumsq time). Structural problems are supposed to error in both layers per the house rule.
findings.evidence: d=3: backend probe_kind(len-5 weight) constructs (weight.shape (5,1)); sumsq equals the len-3 truncation (1224.899503 both); probe_derivatives_kind((5,3)) likewise equals w2[:3]; len-2 weight -> IndexError at sumsq. Frontend rejects both with a clear ValueError. Aliasing is safe on both layers (shares_memory False; mutation after build does not change the objective).

findings.title: Armijo exhaustion accepts the last trial silently; recorded alpha is one halving past the step taken
findings.claim: newton_cg's line search runs 40 backtracks and, if none satisfies Armijo, accepts x_trial anyway with no failure signal; the loop halves alpha after the last trial, so the NewtonInfo row records alpha=2^-40 while x_trial/f_new were computed at 2^-39, making delta_f/predicted/rho/step_rel on that row describe a step not taken. gradient_descent does the same with 50 backtracks and records nothing. Demonstrated at the precision floor (a warm-start/continuation run with a never-triggering Newton stop): objective increases were accepted.
findings.evidence: newton_cg gtol_rel=1e-30, 16 iterations: it 12 ls_steps=40 alpha=9.095e-13 delta_f=+3.343e-28; it 13 ls_steps=40 delta_f=+3.229e-27 (accepted increases); 96 objective evaluations. gradient_descent from the floored point: ~25 objective evals/iteration, losses 4.956e-28, 8.944e-28, 1.724e-27, 1.312e-27 (non-monotone), stats keys ['losses','n_iter'] only.
findings.repro_output: 12        40  9.095e-13   +3.343e-28    1.704e-14        25   False | 13        40  9.095e-13   +3.229e-27 ... | accepted an objective INCREASE (delta_f > 0) on an exhausted iteration: True | gradient_descent ... 103 Problem.objective evaluations ... losses: ['4.956e-28', '8.944e-28', '1.724e-27', '1.312e-27']
findings.proposed_fix: On exhaustion keep x (reject the step), add an ls_failed field to NewtonInfo (and a stop or warning), and record the alpha actually used (break before the final halving).
findings.supported_path: newton_cg/gradient_descent with a tiny gtol_rel or a pinned g0norm_newton (docs §5 warm-start advice), or any objective the Armijo test cannot satisfy

findings.title: ut3_squash_tails sums padded boundary-bond slots into the real slot; +, -, squash_tails, sum_stack are not garbage-robust and the corewise optimizer produces that garbage
findings.claim: ut3_squash_tails (and so UniformTuckerTensorTrain.squash_tails, __add__/__sub__ which squash after ut3_add, and sum_stack) calls tt_squash_tails on the raw tt supercore without masking on entry; _tt_squash_tails_uniform sums over ALL r slots of core 0's left leg and core d-1's right leg, so any nonzero value in a padded boundary-bond slot is added into real slot 0 and the represented tensor changes. This violates the equivalence contract's 'garbage padding is don't-care' and prong 3 of the testing strategy. It is reachable from the public API: a point fitted by optimizers.adam(UNIFORM_COREWISE, ...) carries nonzero values in exactly those slots (the corewise gradient is nonzero there, R8-3), after which x_fit + y, x_fit - y, x_fit.squash_tails() and stack(...).sum_stack() return silently wrong tensors while to_dense/norm (which mask first) are right.
findings.evidence: Synthetic garbage: to_dense rel err 0.0 but squash_tails 30.1, x+y 50.9, x-y 59.8, sum_stack 224 (squash_garbage.py); fails in every config of the 3-prong sweep (42/42 for +, 42/42 squash, 36/36 sum_stack; every other op passes). Library path (adam_then_add.py): after adam(UNIFORM_COREWISE,'probe',...,max_iter=50) max|padded boundary-bond slots| = 0.226; vs clean=x_fit.apply_masks(): to_dense 0.0, norm 0.0, but squash_tails 0.372, x_fit+y 0.162, x_fit-y 0.158, sum_stack 0.372; the ragged x_fit.to_t3()+y.to_t3() is 7.7e-17.
findings.repro_output:
x_fit padded boundary-bond slots max |.| : 0.226
to_dense(x_fit) == to_dense(clean)       : 0.0
x_fit.squash_tails() vs clean  rel err   : 0.372
x_fit + y  vs clean + y        rel err   : 0.162
x_fit - y  vs clean - y        rel err   : 0.158
x_fit.to_t3() + y (ragged)     rel err   : 7.68e-17
stack(x_fit,x_fit).sum_stack() rel err   : 0.372
findings.proposed_fix: Mask the boundary legs on entry in ut3_squash_tails (multiply G0 by ttm[0] along axis -3 and Gf by ttm[-1] along axis -1, or ut3_apply_masks the tt supercore) before summing; add the garbage prong for +/-/squash_tails/sum_stack to tests/test_uniform_tucker_tensor_train.py.

findings.title: Corewise transposes are documented as 'clean-padded' but the gradient is nonzero in the padded boundary-bond slots
findings.claim: The section comments at ut3_sampling.py:100-102 and :200-201 say the raw gradient supercores (dU, dG) are 'clean-padded (the masked frame zeros the padding, so the gradient never grows rank into it)'. That holds for every Tucker slot and interior bond, but not for bond 0's left leg (mode 0) and bond d's right leg (mode d-1): the boundary bond is summed, so the derivative w.r.t. a padded boundary slot equals the real-slot derivative and is nonzero. This is what feeds R8-1 through the corewise optimizer.

Dense values agree, but the rank structure differs between layers, and the documented '+ <-> concatenate' weight duality (docs/weighting.md:56; ut3_operations.py:368-369 'the weight-side partner of ut3_add, which concatenates the object's rank masks in exactly the same way') holds in ragged and fails in uniform: the concatenated weight's boundary mask is [1,0,1,0] vs the sum's [1,0,0,0], so ut3_absorb_weights(ux+uy, UWx.concatenate(UWy)) raises the inconsistent-pair ValueError.
findings.evidence: concat_weights_vs_add.py: ragged (x+y).tt_ranks = (2, 4, 4, 2), concat weight tt lengths [2, 4, 4, 2], absorb ok; uniform (x+y) bond-0 mask [1,0,0,0] vs concat weight bond-0 mask [1,0,1,0], absorb -> ValueError 'Inconsistent (UniformTuckerTensorTrain, UT3Weights) pair in absorb_weights'.

ragged: (x+y).tt_ranks = (2, 4, 4, 2) | concat weight tt lengths = [2, 4, 4, 2]
ragged absorb(x+y, Wx.concat(Wy)): ok
uniform: (x+y) tt bond-0 mask [1, 0, 0, 0] | concat weight bond-0 mask [1, 0, 1, 0]

findings.title: NaN jax.grad through uniform weighted norm/inner (default orthogonalized path) and plain ux.norm() on any padded train
findings.claim: `jax.grad` of `ut3_weighted_norm(ux, W)` (default `use_orthogonalization=True`), of `ut3_weighted_inner`, and of plain `UniformTuckerTensorTrain.norm()` returns all-NaN gradients (w.r.t. the train AND w.r.t. the weights) whenever any core has rank slack — i.e. on every realistic uniform train (tight padding with varying ranks, or padded-above for continuation). The NaN originates in the SVD-based uniform left-orthogonalization (`_ut3_left_orthogonalized`) at the padded zero singular values. No error is raised. The ragged twins, the `use_orthogonalization=False` path, the tangent-level `UT3Tangent.weighted_norm/inner` (incl. through `reciprocal`), and a fully uniform-rank train (no slack) are all finite. The pytree registration comment at uniform_tucker_tensor_train.py:1266 explicitly bills the weight supercores as 'float PARAMETERS -- differentiable data', so differentiating the weighted norm is an advertised use. This is a general uniform-orthogonalization property that surfaces on the weighted layer's default path.
findings.evidence: r10_grad.py: ragged grad finite (x and W); uniform[tight] and uniform[padded]: `grad ux.norm()` False, `ut3_weighted_norm(orth=True)` wrt ux False / wrt W False, `(orth=False)` True/True, `ut3_weighted_inner(orth=True)` False; tangent-level all True. r10_grad_uniformrank.py (ranks (3,3,3)/(1,3,3,1), no interior slack): all finite, incl. `_ut3_left_orthogonalized` alone.

uniform[tight] grad ut3_weighted_norm(orth=True)  wrt ux: False | wrt W: False
uniform[tight] grad ut3_weighted_norm(orth=False) wrt ux: True | wrt W: True
uniform[padded] grad ut3_weighted_inner(orth=True) wrt ux: False
