(r10_grad_uniformrank.py) grad ux.norm() finite: True

findings.title: docs/weighting.md `+` <-> `concatenate` duality does not hold for the uniform frontend `+` (it squashes tails); `UT3Weights.concatenate` is the partner of the BACKEND `ut3_add` only
findings.claim: weighting.md states the `+`/`⊙` duality ('`A + B` -> ... weights concatenate (`W_A.concatenate(W_B)`)') and then says `UT3Weights` mirrors it 'the same way'. On ragged this holds with the frontend `x + y` because `TuckerTensorTrain.__add__` returns `t3_add` unsquashed (boundary bonds become 2, matching the concatenated boundary weights). On uniform, `UniformTuckerTensorTrain.__add__` applies `ut3_squash_tails` (uniform_tucker_tensor_train.py:264), so `UW_A.concatenate(UW_B)` is NOT consistent with `ux + uy` (boundary mask rank 1 vs weight width 2; `is_consistent_with` False, `ut3_absorb_weights` raises). It is consistent with the backend `ut3_linalg.ut3_add` and the dense identity holds there. The `UT3Weights.concatenate` docstring (uniform_tucker_tensor_train.py:1139) calls it 'the weight-side partner of `ut3_add`', accurate only at the backend level; nothing tells the user the frontend `+` breaks the pairing, and the concatenated boundary weights cannot survive a squash.
findings.evidence: r10_uniform_equiv.py part A, every structure/stack: 'concat consistent with backend ut3_add: True, with frontend ux+uy: False'; dense `+` identity via backend ut3_add ≤1e-9. r10_identities.py: ragged frontend `x + y` identity 1.2e-15 and `not Wc.is_consistent_with((x+y).squash_tails())`.
findings.repro_output:
struct=(5, 6, 7) ss=(2,)  concat consistent with backend ut3_add: True, with frontend ux+uy: False  ALL OK
struct=(4, 7, 5, 6) ss=(2, 3)  concat consistent with backend ut3_add: True, with frontend ux+uy: False  ALL OK
findings.proposed_fix: In weighting.md's uniform section and the `UT3Weights.concatenate` docstring, state that the uniform duality pairs with the unsquashed backend `ut3_add` (the frontend `+` squashes the boundary bonds) — or absorb before adding; alternatively make the uniform frontend `+` not squash, for ragged parity.

findings.related_known: docs/weighting.md:184,208 (uniform 'same operations' — reverse/stack/unstack) is the known item; this is a different claim on the same page.

findings.title: Ragged tensor-weight ops silently broadcast a mis-stacked T3Weights (uniform rejects); t3_weighted_inner then fails with a bare AssertionError
findings.claim: `t3_absorb_weights` / `t3_weighted_norm` do not enforce `T3Weights.is_consistent_with`: a weight with an extra leading stack `(3,)+C` on a `C`-stacked train is accepted and broadcast to a `(3,2)`-stacked result, and a `()` weight broadcasts over the stack — while `is_consistent_with` returns False and the docstring says the weights 'share the cores' C stack'. `t3_weighted_inner(x, W_big, x, W)` then dies in `t3_inner_product`'s `assert(vsx == vsy)` (t3_linalg.py:195) with no message. The uniform twins reject all three cases with a clear ValueError (`_check_weights_pair`). The broadcast results are numerically correct for what they compute, so this is an inconsistency/ergonomics item, not a wrong answer.
findings.evidence: r10_batching.py: `T3Weights.is_consistent_with(x) W=(3,)+C -> False` yet `t3_absorb_weights` ACCEPTED (result stack (3,2)); `t3_weighted_inner W=(3,)+C REJECTED AssertionError: <no message>`; uniform: `ut3_absorb_weights W=(3,)+C REJECTED ValueError: Inconsistent (UniformTuckerTensorTrain, UT3Weights) pair`.

t3_absorb_weights W=(3,)+C                                 ACCEPTED  (result stack/shape (5, 6, 7))

t3_weighted_inner W=(3,)+C                                 REJECTED  AssertionError: <no message>

findings.title: Shared companion built on a UT3Frame.to_t3frame() leaf gives a silently wrong tied projection
findings.claim: fv_shared_frame_data derives the centers H_i by re-sweeping the left chain with fresh SVDs and pairs them with the stored O_i; on the sliced cores of a UT3Frame.to_t3frame() leaf the sweep's sign/rotation choices differ from the padded construction, so S_i^T = <O_i, H_i> is inconsistent and shared_manifold(spec).project_ambient(leaf, z) returns a tangent that is 32-33% off the true tied projection and does not lie in the tied tangent space (re-projecting it with the correct companion moves it 18-21%). The companion spectrum (gauge-invariant) is still right, so nothing flags it. The docs cover only the opposite direction (t3frame_to_ut3frame-packed frames, docs/uniform_equivalence_contract.md:80-85, sharing_internals.md:134-141); the UT3Frame.to_t3frame route is the one UniformManifoldGeometry.project_ambient's own docstring recommends for dense gradients (uniform_manifold.py:1168-1171), and SharedGeometry.shared_frame_data(frame) is public.
findings.evidence: F (2): for both stack elements c: 'ragged companion on to_t3frame() leaf: spectrum == true' PASS; 'GR.project_ambient(to_t3frame leaf, z) == true tied projection (dense)' FAIL [0.318 / 0.333]; 'leaf result lies in the TRUE tied tangent space (re-projection fixes it)' FAIL [0.180 / 0.213]; the two layers on their OWN frames agree: 'GU.project_ambient == GR.project_ambient per element (dense)' PASS [1.7e-15]. A2 (e): the same mismatch at the coordinate level [1.27].
findings.repro_output:
FAIL (2) c=0 GR.project_ambient(to_t3frame leaf, z) == true tied projection (dense)  [0.3183415346692767]
FAIL (2) c=0 leaf result lies in the TRUE tied tangent space (re-projection fixes it)  [0.1802397218485309]
PASS (1) GU.project_ambient == GR.project_ambient per element (dense)  [1.6714939241716376e-15]
findings.proposed_fix: Build the centers gauge-consistently from STORED cores only: H_i = L_i contracted with the right-chain environment tt_zipper_right_to_left(left[i+1:], right[i+1:]) (no fresh SVD, no sign freedom; the frame is consistent by construction), which also removes the 'as stored, not re-masked' fragility. At minimum document the reverse caveat and have fv_shared_frame_data verify the re-swept right chain matches the stored one.

findings.title: Negative axis in UT3Variations.sum_stack / sum_tangents hits the mode axis (silent when K == d)
findings.claim: ufv_variations_sum_stack (line 195) and utv_sum_tangent_stack (utv_operations.py:169) map axis to array axis 1+axis, so axis=-1 selects array axis 0 = the mode index d. findings.title: numpy-integer shape entries on a uniform point crash newton_cg(use_jit=True) with a deep TracerArrayConversionError
findings.claim: `_is_static_leaf` classifies only Python `int`/`bool` as static structure, so a `UniformTuckerTensorTrain` whose `shape` tuple holds numpy integers (e.g. `tuple(np.array(shape))`, which the dataclass constructor and `validate()` accept) has those entries turned into TRACED leaves by `partition_static` when the backend frame tuple crosses the `_jitted(_cg_core)` boundary; host shape arithmetic then fails deep inside with `TracerArrayConversionError`. A numpy-array `shape` fails even at `jax.jit(lambda u: u.norm())` with jax's obscure 'Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields'. Eager runs and the frontend jit of `norm` (numpy-int tuple) work, so the failure is jit-only and far from the cause. Library constructors already canonicalize (`ut3_constructors.py:103 tuple(int(Ni) ...)`); the dataclass path does not.
findings.evidence: partition_static of a uniform frame: 4 dynamic leaves with Python-int shape, 7 with np.int64 shape (the 3 shape entries became leaves). newton_cg(UNIFORM_MANIFOLD,'apply',...,u_npint64,use_jit=True) -> TracerArrayConversionError: The numpy.ndarray conversion method __array__() was called on traced array with shape int32[]; with shape=np.array -> jit(norm) raises ValueError 'Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields'; with a list shape everything works; eager newton_cg works for all.
findings.repro_output:
tuple(np.int64)  constructs; jit(norm) OK; newton_cg(use_jit) raises TracerArrayConversionError: The numpy.ndarray conversion method __array__() was called on traced array with shape int32[]
np.array         constructs; jit(norm) raises ValueError: Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields ; newton_cg(use_jit) raises TracerArrayConversionError
shape as np.int64 entries -> dynamic leaves: 7 vs Python ints: 4
findings.proposed_fix: Canonicalize `shape` to `tuple(int(s) for s in shape)` in the `UniformTuckerTensorTrain` / `UT3Frame` / `UT3Variations` validation (as `ut3_constructors.py:103` already does), and/or accept `np.integer`/`np.bool_` scalars as static in `_is_static_leaf` (`isinstance(x, (bool, int, np.integer, np.bool_))`).
findings.supported_path: User constructs `UniformTuckerTensorTrain(tk, tt, shape, masks)` directly (documented constructor; `shape` documented as Tuple[int,...]) with a numpy-derived shape, then `optimizers.newton_cg(..., use_jit=True)`. Marginal but reachable with documented inputs.
findings.lane: H1 — jit identity and cache keys

findings.title: jax-array masks pass UT3Masks validation but cannot be a jit cache key (unhashable ArrayImpl / obscure pytree-metadata error)
findings.claim: `UniformTuckerTensorTrain.validate` checks masks with `is_boolean_ndarray`, which accepts jax boolean arrays, and `require_concrete_masks` rejects only tracers, so a `UT3Masks` built from `jnp` arrays is accepted, validates, and runs eagerly (including eager `newton_cg`). But `UniformManifoldGeometryOps.from_point` / `Uniform*Kind.from_point` store those arrays in value-hashed fields, and `ValueHashedFields._value_key` (common.py:541) only handles `np.ndarray`; a jax array falls through to `hash(jax_array)` -> `TypeError: unhashable type: 'jaxlib._jax.ArrayImpl'`, and `newton_cg(use_jit=True)` surfaces as jax's 'Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields of pytree'. (`ValueHashedMasks` happens to work because jax arrays have `.tobytes()`, so the frontend-only jit path does not catch it.) Masks are documented HOST numpy, so this is an unhelpful error on an off-contract input, not a wrong answer.
findings.evidence: UT3Masks(jnp masks): validate accepts; to_jax() keeps masks numpy (good); UniformManifoldGeometryOps.from_point(uj.data) + hash -> TypeError unhashable ArrayImpl; newton_cg(use_jit=True) -> ValueError 'Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields of pytree. Make sure that metadata fields are hashable...'; newton_cg eager OK. Also identity_matrix.py: 'jax masks in a kind field: hash raises TypeError'.
findings.repro_output:
validate accepts jax masks
from_point/hash raises TypeError: unhashable type: 'jaxlib._jax.ArrayImpl'
newton_cg(use_jit) raises ValueError: Exception raised while checking equality of metadata fields of pytree. Make sure that metadata fields are hashable and h
newton_cg(eager) OK
findings.proposed_fix: Require `isinstance(m, np.ndarray)` (host numpy) in the validation of `UT3Masks`/`UT3FrameMasks`/`UT3VariationsMasks` (or the owning objects' `validate`), reusing the `require_concrete_masks` wording; alternatively `np.asarray` the masks in the holders' `__post_init__`. Optionally make `_value_key` convert jax arrays via `np.asarray` so user-built kinds/geometries fail clearly or work.
findings.supported_path: Off-contract input (masks documented as HOST numpy) that the structural validation nevertheless accepts; reached by `UT3Masks(jnp.asarray(...))` then `newton_cg(..., use_jit=True)` or any `from_point`.
findings.lane: H1 — jit identity and cache keys

findings.title: ValueHashedFields caches its key; uniform geometries/kinds alias the point's writeable mask arrays, so in-place mutation after first hash goes unseen
findings.claim: `ValueHashedFields._fields_key` is a `cached_property`, so the value key is computed once. `UniformManifoldGeometryOps.from_point` / `UniformCorewiseGeometryOps.from_point` / `_UniformKind.from_point` store `tuple(base_masks)` — the SAME writeable arrays as `x0.masks.data` — so a user mutating a mask in place after the geometry/kind has been hashed leaves a stale key: it keeps hashing/comparing equal to the ORIGINAL content and unequal to its own current content. `_weight_matrix` already defends its array (copy + `setflags(write=False)`, fitting.py:229); the masks do not. No library code writes masks in place (grep), so this needs user mutation — a latent sharp edge, not a supported-path bug.
findings.evidence: hash(um1) before/after mutating its held mask array unchanged; um1 == fresh(original content) -> True; um1 == fresh(mutated content) -> False; x.masks.data[0].flags.writeable -> True.
findings.repro_output:
mutated-after-hash: hash unchanged = True ; equals a fresh object with the MUTATED content = False ; equals a fresh object with the ORIGINAL content = True
OK   stored masks are writeable (not frozen via setflags)
findings.proposed_fix: In the `from_point` constructors (and/or the three mask holders' `__post_init__`) store `np.array(m, copy=True)` with `setflags(write=False)`, mirroring `_weight_matrix`.

findings.title: ValueHashedMasks eq/hash contract: bool vs int8 masks with the same content compare equal but hash differently
findings.claim: `ValueHashedMasks.__eq__` uses `np.array_equal` (dtype-blind) while `_content_hash` includes `dtype.str`, so `UT3Masks(bool)` == `UT3Masks(int8, same content)` is True with unequal hashes — a violation of the hash/eq contract. Consequence is only a cache miss, and `UniformTuckerTensorTrain.validate` rejects non-bool masks, so only a bare holder exhibits it.
findings.evidence: UT3Masks bool vs int8 same content: eq = True , hash equal = False
findings.repro_output: UT3Masks bool vs int8 same content: eq = True , hash equal = False
findings.proposed_fix: Compare `a.dtype == b.dtype and np.array_equal(a, b)` in `__eq__` (or drop dtype from the hash).

findings.title: Problem.objective/local_model silently discard data= when sample is omitted
findings.claim: Both `Problem.local_model(x, sample=None, data=None)` (:178-181) and `Problem.objective(x, sample=None, data=None)` (:191-197) begin with `if sample is None: sample, data = self.sample, self.data`, so a caller who passes `data=` alone (the documented keyword, meaning 'score the full sample against these values') gets the objective/model on the TRAINING data with no error. findings.title: rank_adjustment_sweep('right_to_left') is documented as right-orthogonal but leaves the Tucker cores non-orthogonal
findings.claim: Five doc sites promise that `rank_adjustment_sweep('right_to_left')` returns a right-orthogonal T3 (backend t3_svd.py:301; tucker_tensor_train.py:4452; `is_right_orthogonal` docstring :791 which also says to use it before `t3svd(assume_orthogonal=True)`; uniform_tucker_tensor_train.py:724; docs/t3svd_minimal_ranks.md:74). On a generic (non-left-orthogonal) input the sweep's `t3_down_svd_tt_core` step pushes the non-orthogonal factor up into the Tucker cores, so only the TT cores come out right-orthogonal and `is_right_orthogonal()` is False. Following the documented chain `x.rank_adjustment_sweep('right_to_left').t3svd(max_tt_ranks=2, assume_orthogonal=True)` therefore truncates wrongly, silently. Incidental to this lane (found by the twin sweep), outside its bug class.

On a left-orthogonal input (t3svd output) the same sweep IS right-orthogonal (True). Truncation error: x.t3svd(max_tt_ranks=2) 0.1652 vs the documented chain 0.2156 at identical ranks (1,2,2,1). Uniform twin: same non-orthogonality.

findings.proposed_fix: Either make the sweep genuinely right-orthogonal (orthogonalize each Tucker core after its bond step, e.g. a down-orthogonalization of the Tucker core whose remainder is absorbed into the TT core before the right SVD), or reword all five sites to 'TT cores right-orthogonal; full right-orthogonal form only for a left-orthogonal input' and remove the assume_orthogonal chain advice from is_right_orthogonal.

findings.title: UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.transport / project_ambient crash for a tangent-stacked (K != ()) UT3Tangent; the ragged twin handles the same K+C-vs-C broadcast
findings.claim: utv_project_ut3_onto_tangent_space builds the gauge masks from the frame (stack C, via ufv_variation_masks) but the ungauged variations dB/dG it computes inherit the projected tensor's stack (K+C when x_data is K-stacked); it then passes (dB, dG, shape, C-masks) to utv_orthogonal_gauge_projection, whose ufv_apply_variations_masks reshapes the C-stacked masks to (d,)+ss+... with ss = K+C read off the supercore and raises 'cannot reshape array'. Because UniformManifoldGeometry.transport(v, new_frame) is project_ambient(new_frame, v.to_ut3()) and v.to_ut3() carries K+C, transport of ANY tangent-stacked uniform tangent crashes, as does project_ambient with a K-stacked uniform gradient at an unstacked/C frame. The ragged MANIFOLD.transport and MANIFOLD.project_ambient accept the identical inputs and return the per-element-correct result (verified for every (C,K) in the sweep). The UT3Tangent class docstring advertises the K stack and UniformManifoldGeometry.transport's docstring carries no K restriction; tests/test_uniform_manifold.py:1177 test_transport explicitly tests 'No K'.

Fails for d=2,3,4 and every K != () in sweep_uniform.py (20 cases), traceback through utv_operations.py:575 -> :446 -> ufv_masking.py:154.

ragged project_ambient(frame C=(), grad K+C=(2,)) -> (2,)
uniform project_ambient RAISES ValueError cannot reshape array of size 9 into shape (3,2,3,1)
uniform transport with K=() -> (5, 6, 7)

The elementwise-multiply parity gap itself is already cataloged; the finding is only the missing type check.

findings.repro_output: UniformTuckerTensorTrain * UniformTuckerTensorTrain -> RAISES ValueError: 'all the input arrays must have same number of dimensions, but the array at index 0 has 3 dimension(s) and the array at i...'
findings.proposed_fix: Raise TypeError('UniformTuckerTensorTrain.__mul__ scales by a scalar only; elementwise multiplication has no uniform twin') when the operand is not a scalar.

findings.title: COREWISE.retract accepts a MANIFOLD-frame tangent unchecked: raw broadcast error on a slack frame (nU != nD), silently wrong-typed arithmetic on a minimal one
findings.claim: CorewiseGeometry.retract documents 'p must be a corewise tangent (a frame from frame)' but does not check it. With an orthogonal frame that has slack between its rank stores (up_ranks (2,3,4) vs down_ranks (2,3,3), produced by t3_orthogonal_representations of a non-minimal x, the asymmetric structure the brief asks for) the additive retraction raises 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,7) (3,7)'; with a minimal orthogonal frame the same misuse silently adds manifold variations to (U, P). Not a stacking bug (identical for every C, K); recorded because the stacked sweep tripped on it and the silent half is the dangerous one. The backend CorewiseGeometryOps.retract has the same gap.
findings.evidence: repro_misc_stack.py: slack frame up_ranks (2,3,4) down_ranks (2,3,3); MANIFOLD.retract(v at slack frame) -> ((2,3,3),(1,2,3,1)); COREWISE.retract(v at slack MANIFOLD frame) -> RAISES ValueError 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,7) (3,7)'. tracebacks.py: same call on a minimal frame returns a TuckerTensorTrain without error.
findings.repro_output:
slack frame up_ranks (2, 3, 4) down_ranks (2, 3, 3)
MANIFOLD.retract(v at slack frame) -> ((2, 3, 3), (1, 2, 3, 1))
COREWISE.retract(v at slack MANIFOLD frame) -> RAISES ValueError: 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,7) (3,7) '
findings.proposed_fix: In CorewiseGeometry.retract (and CorewiseGeometryOps.retract) require a corewise frame (down/left/right cores identical, or at least nU == nD per mode) and raise a ValueError naming the geometry mismatch.
findings.supported_path: COREWISE.retract(p) where p.frame came from MANIFOLD.frame / t3_orthogonal_representations (a geometry mix-up the docstring forbids but nothing checks)

findings.title: numerical_contracts.md lists shared(...).frame(x) as a TIED precondition; the code ties silently
findings.claim: The row '`shared(…)` wrapper: `frame(x)`, `transport(v, new_frame)` | **TIED** (the point / the new frame)' says safe mode raises when shared(...).frame is given an untied point. The code (and CHANGELOG.md:159-162, 'Entering the format is the geometry's job... ties an untied x first, silently') does not raise: frame(x) projects the point onto the tied set by the per-group mean. Only transport (new frame) actually checks TIED.

findings.repro_output:
OK shared.frame untied (TIED) -- CHANGELOG says ties silently: doc says no check -> no raise
OK shared.transport to untied frame (TIED): doc says raises -> RAISED ValueError
OK t3svd(sharing) untied (TIED): doc says raises -> RAISED ValueError
findings.proposed_fix: Split the row: `frame(x)` — '— (ties the point first; an untied point is silently projected by the per-group mean)'; keep TIED for `transport(v, new_frame)`.

findings.title: ut3_squash_tails sums the raw (unmasked) boundary bonds: squash_tails, +, -, sum_stack, UT3Frame.allclose/is_consistent read padding garbage
findings.claim: ut3_squash_tails calls tt_squash_tails on the unmasked tt supercore, so the padded slots of the leading bond of core 0 and the trailing bond of core d-1 are summed into the real slot 0. Every frontend op routed through it -- UniformTuckerTensorTrain.squash_tails, __add__, __sub__, sum_stack, and via __sub__ also UT3Frame.allclose and UT3Frame.is_consistent -- returns a wrong tensor whenever the input's boundary-bond padding is nonzero, which the equivalence contract declares don't-care. A user reaches it without raw construction: UNIFORM_COREWISE.randn(frame) fills the whole padded variation supercore (documented) and UNIFORM_COREWISE.retract adds it raw into the point; the retracted point's to_dense/norm/sampling are right but y + z, y - z, y.squash_tails(), stack([y,y]).sum_stack() are wrong by O(1).
findings.evidence: repro_squash_public_path.py: retracted point tt[0] left-bond padding nonzero -> (y+z).to_dense() vs y.to_dense()+z.to_dense() relerr 1.622e+00; (y-z) 1.618; (y+y) vs 2y 1.624; y.squash_tails() 1.624; stack([y,y]).sum_stack() 1.624; y.norm() 1.6e-16 (masks on entry). Backend: new G0[0] == sum over ALL padded left-bond slots (True) vs sum over MASKED slots (False); squashing the masked data gives the right tensor. repro_garbage_ut3.py: the same four ops fail (relerr 1e5..1e6 with 1e3 garbage) in all 16 structure/padding configs while every other op is inert; repro_tangent.py: frame.allclose / frame.is_consistent FAIL on a garbage-padded, real-identical orthogonal frame.
findings.repro_output: (y + z).to_dense() vs y.to_dense()+z.to_dense(): relerr = 1.622e+00 | y.squash_tails().to_dense() vs y.to_dense(): relerr = 1.624e+00 | backend ut3_squash_tails: new G0[0] == sum over ALL padded left-bond slots (garbage included)? True ; == sum over MASKED slots? False
findings.proposed_fix: In ut3_squash_tails multiply the two boundary bonds by their masks (ttm[0] on core 0's left axis, ttm[-1] on core d-1's right axis) before tt_squash_tails, or call ut3_apply_masks first. Add squash_tails/+/-/sum_stack to a garbage-robustness test (test_padding_is_dont_care only corrupts the Tucker padding and only checks to_dense).
findings.supported_path: UNIFORM_COREWISE.randn(frame) -> UNIFORM_COREWISE.retract -> y + z / y.squash_tails() / sum_stack (all documented); or any raw-.data UniformTuckerTensorTrain (contract: padding is don't-care)

findings.title: ut3_orthogonal_representations on a non-minimal-rank point: frame masks from a right-then-left rank recurrence do not match the left-then-right sweep; left/down masks too restrictive, frame non-orthogonal, tangent space wrong
findings.claim: The uniform frame masks are built from ranks.compute_orthogonal_representation_ranks (ranks.py:496; right chain reduced at :554, left chain derived from the reduced right ranks at :564 -- the paper's right-then-left order), but the sweep actually run, fv_conversions.t3_orthogonal_representations, is left-then-right (the documented Algorithm-11 divergence): its left chain keeps min(rL*n, r_{i+1}) against the ORIGINAL bond. At a non-minimal TT bond the left chain and the down core (whose left leg is the left bond) hold more orthonormal content than the mask admits. The masked down core is then not orthonormal, UT3Frame.is_orthogonal() is False for the library's own frame, safe mode rejects every manifold op on it with an unfixable 'requires an orthogonal frame', and in unsafe mode / under jit project_ambient, transport, inner/norm and retract compute in a smaller-than-true tangent space. CLAUDE.md and docs/uniform_equivalence_contract.md state the contract holds on non-minimal input and that minimal rank is a precondition for nothing; x + y (always non-minimal) is the everyday input.
findings.evidence: repro_nonminimal_rootcause.py, x=randn((5,7,6),(2,3,2),(1,2,3,1)): formula left ranks (1,2,2,1) vs ragged T3Frame.from_t3 actual left ranks (1,2,3,1); uniform left core 1 unmasked Gram over bond 2 = identity 3x3 (mask keeps 2); down core 2 masked 2-row Gram = [[0.9955,-0.0068],[-0.0068,0.9897]] -> is_orthogonal() False; MANIFOLD.norm(v)=5.745542 vs dense HS norm 5.737065; project_ambient(frame(x), z) uniform vs ragged relerr 3.682e-02 (the projection is unique); safe mode: UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.randn(UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame(x)) raises 'requires an orthogonal frame'; frame(x+y).is_orthogonal() False while ragged T3Frame.from_t3(x+y).is_orthogonal() True. repro_nonminimal_frame.py: same on the uniform_fitting doctest's non-minimal example (residual 2.1e-2); minimal control and non-minimal Tucker case are fine. repro_gappy.py: frame(x+y) non-orthogonal in every structure (residuals 1.4e-4..2.1e-1).
findings.repro_output: formula compute_orthogonal_representation_ranks: left (1,2,2,1); ragged actual left (1,2,3,1) | uniform left core 1 unmasked Gram (bond 2) = I_3, mask keeps 2 | masked down core 2 Gram [[0.9955,-0.0068],[-0.0068,0.9897]] -> is_orthogonal() = False | MANIFOLD.norm(v)=5.745542 vs HS 5.737065 | project_ambient uniform vs ragged relerr 3.682e-02 | frame(x + y).is_orthogonal() = False
findings.proposed_fix: Make the mask builder follow the sweep it masks: compute frame ranks with the left-then-right recurrence (left_{i+1} = min(left_i * n_i, r_{i+1}) on the original bonds, right from the left chain, down from both) or run the sweep right-then-left so the existing formula is correct. Add a non-minimal structure and an x+y point to test_uniform_manifold _CONFIGS with frame.is_orthogonal() and project_ambient-vs-ragged assertions.

findings.title: Minimal-rank but slack-padded x0 passes uniform_minimal yet every uniform manifold optimizer crashes: ut3svd/utv_retract shrink the padded dims to max(raw ranks), desyncing the loop-invariant masks; utv_retract docstring 'output at the frame padded dims' is false
findings.claim: ut3svd slices its output to n2 = max(raw_tucker), r2 = max(raw_tt) (ut3_svd.py:111-116), so utv_retract returns a UT3 whose padded dims are the max real ranks, not the frame's padded dims -- contradicting its docstring (utv_operations.py:326-328: 'the output is a UT3 at the frame padded dims ... so no extra slice is needed'). The optimizers hold x0's masks loop-invariant and only check rank minimality (uniform_fitting.py:431), so a minimal-rank x0 built with the documented from_t3(x, n=, r=) 'force a larger pad' option passes uniform_minimal unchanged and then newton_cg, mc_sgd, adam and backend gradient_descent all crash at the second step with a bare numpy broadcast error (the corewise geometry, additive retraction, is fine).
findings.evidence: repro_slack_padding_optimizer.py: x0 padded n=5 r=4 (max real ranks 3,2): minimal? True; uniform_minimal returns same object; frontend retract of the zero tangent: output (n,r)=(3,2), frame (nU,rL)=(5,4), x0 (n,r)=(5,4); newton_cg / mc_sgd / adam / backend gradient_descent CRASH ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with remapped shapes ... (3,3,7) ... (3,5); newton_cg COREWISE OK; tight padding n=3 r=2: everything OK. repro_tangent.py flags 'retract output padded dims == frame padded dims (docstring claim) FAIL got n,r=3,2 frame nU,rL=5,5' on every forced-pad config.
findings.repro_output: x0 padded n=5 r=4 (max real ranks 3,2); minimal? True; uniform_minimal returns same object? True | frontend retract of zero tangent: output (n, r) = (3, 2); frame (nU, rL) = (5, 4) | newton_cg CRASH ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with remapped shapes [original->remapped]: (3,3,7)->(3,3,7) (3,5)->(3,5,newaxis) ...
findings.proposed_fix: Either keep the input padded dims in utv_retract (skip the [:n2]/[:r2] slice on the retract path -- the masks already carry the ranks) or make uniform_least_squares_problem / the frontend optimizers reject or re-pad a slack-padded x0 (x0.n > max(tucker_ranks) or x0.r > max(tt_ranks)) with a clear message; fix the utv_retract docstring either way.
findings.supported_path: UniformTuckerTensorTrain.from_t3(x, n=..., r=...) (documented 'pass to force a larger pad') -> newton_cg/mc_sgd/adam(UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, ...)
findings.related_known: uniform_fitting.uniform_minimal / 'must start minimal' docs cover rank minimality only, not padding slack
findings.lane: H5 — uniform masks: phantom rank and garbage

findings.title: safety.frames_equal compares raw frame supercores including padding, so real-identical frames with different padding are 'different tangent spaces'
findings.claim: frames_equal / frames_equal_or_skip flatten frame.data[:4] and allclose the full padded supercores. Two uniform frames that are identical on their masked (real) content but differ in the don't-care padding are reported as different frames, so UT3Tangent.__sub__/__add__/allclose/stack_tangents raise the same-tangent-space error. Only reachable by raw construction or by mixing a frame with a re-padded copy, so low priority.
findings.evidence: repro_tangent.py: a garbage-padded copy of an orthogonal frame (is_orthogonal True, to_dense equal, real content bit-identical) -> 'tangent.allclose (dirty vs clean) -- same-frame guard on padding? FAIL raises: Tangent vectors are in different tangent spaces (their frames are not the same frame).' in every config.
findings.repro_output: tangent.allclose (dirty vs clean) -- same-frame guard on padding? FAIL raises: Tangent vectors are in different tangent spaces (their frames are not the same frame).
findings.proposed_fix: Mask both uniform frames (ufv_apply_frame_masks) before the compare at the uniform call sites (UT3Tangent._check_same_tangent_space, stack_tangents), or document that uniform frame equality is on the stored supercores including padding.
findings.lane: H5 — uniform masks: phantom rank and garbage

findings.title: UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame(x) returns a non-orthonormal frame when a TT core's right unfolding is rank-deficient
findings.claim: ut3_orthogonal_representations (reached via UT3Frame.from_ut3 at uniform_frame_variations_format.py:296 and UniformManifoldGeometry.frame at uniform_manifold.py:1027) produces a frame whose down core is not orthonormal when the input x has a TT rank exceeding what the right unfolding can support (r_{i+1} > n_i*r_{i+2}, e.g. the last core with r_{d-1} > n_{d-1}). The ragged twin MANIFOLD.frame(x) is orthonormal on the same x. In safe mode every uniform manifold op on that frame then raises the ORTH precondition with a message telling the user to build the frame with UniformManifoldGeometry.frame (what they did); under safety.unsafe()/jit the ops proceed and UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.project_ambient differs from the ragged result by 1e-2..1e-1 relative, breaking docs/uniform_equivalence_contract.md:33 (the contract holds on non-minimal-rank input too). Left-deficient cases (r1 > n0, r2 > r1*n1), minimal ranks and non-minimal Tucker ranks are fine.
findings.evidence: x = randn((4,5,3),(2,3,2),(1,2,3,1)): ragged frame orthogonality residual 8e-16; UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame(from_t3(x)) residual 2.5e-1, is_orthogonal False (to_t3frame(): down core D[2] gram deviation 0.99); UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.randn(frame) raises 'UniformManifoldGeometry.project requires an orthogonal frame ... Build the frame with UniformManifoldGeometry.frame'. ((3,3,3,3),(2,2,2,2),(1,2,2,3,1)): residual 6.6e-2. Under safety.unsafe(): |ragged project_ambient - uniform project_ambient| / |ragged| = 1.1e-2 and 1.1e-1 on these two structures, 5.8e-16 on minimal ranks.
findings.repro_output:
r2=3 > n2=2 (last core right-deficient)  ragged orth 8e-16 | uniform orth residual 2.5e-01 is_orth=False | unsafe project_ambient ragged-vs-uniform rel diff 1.1e-02
r3=3 > n3*r4=2 (right unfolding deficient)  ragged orth 1e-15 | uniform orth residual 6.6e-02 is_orth=False | unsafe project_ambient ragged-vs-uniform rel diff 1.1e-01
minimal  ragged orth 1e-15 | uniform orth residual 8.9e-16 is_orth=True | rel diff 5.8e-16
findings.proposed_fix: Make the right/down uniform orthogonalization sweep rank-aware like the left sweep (SVD-prefix completion at the zero-sigma slots), or reduce x to minimal structural ranks inside UT3Frame.from_ut3; at minimum raise a clear structural error there (as backend/uniform_fitting.py:431 already does for fitting).
findings.supported_path: UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame(UniformTuckerTensorTrain.from_t3(x)) for any x with a right-rank-deficient TT core, then UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.project/project_ambient/retract/randn (raise in safe mode; wrong values under safety.unsafe() or jit)
findings.related_known: docs/uniform_equivalence_contract.md:33 claims non-minimal input is covered; backend/uniform_fitting.py:431 guards fitting only

findings.title: GAUGE precondition thresholds an absolute gauge residual at the relative tolerance (scale-dependent false failures and false passes)
findings.claim: is_gauged compares tv_gauge_residual (max |U^T V|, which scales linearly with the variation magnitude; backend/tv_operations.py:603) against atol, and the check sites (manifold.py:1296-1301 inner, 1314-1319 norm; uniform_manifold.py:1113-1137) pass safety.effective_rtol (a relative tolerance, 1e-9 numpy / 1e-5 jax) as that atol. A correctly gauged tangent therefore fails MANIFOLD.norm/inner once its norm is large (>= ~1e8 in numpy, >= ~1e2 in jax eager float32, the documented jax-but-not-jit prototyping use), while a tiny ungauged tangent passes and MANIFOLD.norm returns a value that is not the HS norm. ORTH (gram vs identity) and TIED (relative by construction) residuals do not have this problem.
findings.evidence: v = MANIFOLD.randn(frame); w = v*s keeps the gauge exactly (relative residual 1.5e-16 at every scale) but MANIFOLD.norm(w) raises 'requires gauged variations' at s=1e8 (residual 9.3e-8) and 1e10 in numpy; in jax eager float32 it raises already at s=1e2 (residual 1.8e-5 > 1e-5). Conversely an ungauged random tangent * 1e-10 has residual 2.5e-10 <= 1e-9, is_gauged() True, and MANIFOLD.norm returns 7.015e-10 while the true HS norm of the realized tensor is 6.779e-10 (ratio 1.035).
findings.repro_path: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-nick-repos-T3Toolbox/7a6ed361-8c79-489c-87ff-713bf71ecb11/scratchpad/repros/H6/repro_gauge_scale.py (jax-eager block at the end of repro_catalog_ragged.py)
findings.repro_output:
scale 1e+08: gauge_residual=9.31e-08 (rel=1.5e-16) MANIFOLD.norm -> RAISES ManifoldGeometry.norm requires gauged variations
same tangent * 1e-10: is_gauged = True residual=2.50e-10 ; MANIFOLD.norm(tiny ungauged) = 7.014590e-10 ; true HS norm = 6.778808e-10 ; ratio = 1.0348
jax eager scale 1e+02: gauge_residual=1.77e-05 rel=3.7e-08 -> MANIFOLD.norm RAISES (gauge)
findings.proposed_fix: Make tv_gauge_residual / utv_gauge_residual relative (divide by the per-stack-element variation norm, matching t3_sharing_residual), or threshold at rtol * corewise_norm inside is_gauged; document the residual as relative.
findings.supported_path: MANIFOLD.norm / MANIFOLD.inner (and the uniform twins) on any gauged tangent of norm >= 1e8 in numpy or >= 1e2 under jax eager float32; geometry.inner is used by the optimizers' CG in eager mode

findings.title: docs/numerical_contracts.md lists shared(...).frame(x) as a TIED precondition; the code ties an untied x silently
findings.claim: The shared-surface table row says the shared wrapper's frame(x) requires TIED factors (safe mode raises), but SharedGeometry.frame (t3toolbox/shared_geometry.py:165-181) deliberately ties an untied point by the per-group mean first and never checks; verified for both the ragged and uniform bases.
findings.evidence: shared_manifold((0,0,1)).frame(untied randn((4,4,3),(2,2,2),(1,2,2,1))) -> safe=pass unsafe=pass (catalog: raise); shared(UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, sh).frame(untied) -> safe=pass. The transport(v, new_frame) half of the same row does raise as documented.
findings.repro_output: shared.frame(untied x)  [doc: TIED]   safe=pass   unsafe=pass   (catalog: raise)   <-- MISMATCH vs catalog
findings.proposed_fix: Move frame(x) out of the TIED row (document it as an entry point that ties silently, like x.share), keeping transport(v, new_frame) there.

findings.title: A structural tangent mismatch is only caught by the numerical same-frame guard; under unsafe()/jit it silently broadcasts
findings.claim: T3Tangent._check_same_tangent_space (and fitting._require_at_frame at fitting.py:108) has no unconditional structural check of the two frames' variation shapes; tangents at frames of different rank structure are rejected only by the numerical frames_equal compare, with a message advising 'run inside safety.unsafe() to skip this numerical check'. Following that advice, a + b with broadcastable holes returns a T3Tangent of a's structure with no error and a.corewise_inner(b) returns a number; with non-broadcastable holes it fails with a raw numpy/jax broadcast error. This contradicts the documented rule that structural problems always error in both modes (docs/user_guide.rst:325, CLAUDE.md). The uniform twin is fine because its mask-equality check is structural and always runs.
findings.evidence: frames with holes ((2,4),(2,5),(2,3))/((1,2,2),(2,2,2),(2,2,1)) vs ((1,4),(1,5),(1,3))/((1,1,1),...): safe mode a+b raises 'Tangent vectors are in different tangent spaces ... run inside safety.unsafe() to skip this numerical check'; under safety.unsafe() a+b -> NO ERROR (result structure = A's), corewise_inner(a,b) = -1.30888. Non-broadcastable case: unsafe -> 'operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)', jit -> TypeError; GaussNewtonModel.gn_quadratic(p of other structure) under unsafe -> raw einsum 'Size of label i ... does not match'.
findings.repro_output:
(3) different-structure tangents with BROADCASTABLE holes, unsafe mode
    unsafe a+b -> NO ERROR, result structure = A's; corewise_inner(a,b) = -1.30888472501278
findings.proposed_fix: In _check_same_tangent_space and _require_at_frame compare frame.variation_shapes (and frame stack shapes) unconditionally before the numerical frames_equal compare, raising a structural message without the unsafe-mode hint.
findings.supported_path: T3Tangent + / - / corewise_inner between tangents of different rank structure inside safety.unsafe() or under jit (user error, but the documented contract says it errors)

findings.title: T3Frame.validate Tucker-rank mismatch message prints the wrong numbers for stacked frames
findings.claim: The condition tests U.shape[-2] == L.shape[-2] == R.shape[-2] but the message formats U.shape[0], L.shape[1], R.shape[1], which are stack dimensions when the frame is stacked, so the error names values that are not the mismatched ranks.

findings.title: set_default_safety(None, None) is accepted and then every precondition check crashes with a TypeError
findings.claim: There is no script-level way to make unsafe the default (unsafe() is only a context manager) and set_default_safety does not validate its arguments: set_default_safety(None, None) stores SafetyTolerances(None, None), checks_active stays True, effective_rtol returns None, and the first check site fails deep inside with a TypeError instead of either skipping checks or rejecting the call.
findings.evidence: After safety.set_default_safety(None, None): current_safety() = SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=None, rtol_jax=None), checks_active(np.zeros(3)) = True, MANIFOLD.norm(v) -> TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'.
findings.repro_output:
current_safety after set_default_safety(None, None): SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=None, rtol_jax=None)
MANIFOLD.norm -> TypeError '<=' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'
findings.proposed_fix: Treat None as unsafe in set_default_safety (mirroring the ContextVar's own None-means-unsafe convention) or validate the tolerances as positive floats.
findings.supported_path: safety.set_default_safety(None, None) then any safe-mode checked op

findings.title: set_default_safety's 'script-level default' is not inherited by threads
findings.claim: The docstring says to use set_default_safety 'for a script-level default', but ContextVar.set applies to the calling context only: a threading.Thread started afterwards sees the library defaults, so a threaded script (e.g. a ThreadPoolExecutor driving fits) silently runs with different tolerances than the main thread set. asyncio tasks do inherit.
findings.evidence: main thread after set_default_safety(1e-3, 1e-2): SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=0.001, rtol_jax=0.01); a worker thread started afterwards reports SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=1e-09, rtol_jax=1e-05).
findings.repro_output:
main thread after set_default_safety: SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=0.001, rtol_jax=0.01)
worker thread sees                  : SafetyTolerances(rtol_numpy=1e-09, rtol_jax=1e-05)
findings.proposed_fix: Document the per-context scope (threads do not inherit) or back the ContextVar with a module-level default that set_default_safety changes.

findings.title: T3Tangent.__add__/__sub__ docstrings still describe the retired identity guard ('same T3Frame object')
findings.claim: The docstrings at manifold.py:371 and :376 say 'Requires both to share the same T3Frame object', but the guard is the numerical frames_equal compare (a value-equal but different frame object passes, as the jit round-trip requires and as the module docstring states).
findings.evidence: gn_hessian(p at SAME frame, value-equal copy) safe=pass; repro_catalog_ragged.py builds a T3Frame from copied arrays of the model frame and the SF-guarded ops accept it.
findings.repro_output: gn_hessian(p at SAME frame, value-equal copy)        safe=pass   unsafe=pass   (catalog: free)
findings.proposed_fix: Reword to 'Requires both tangents to be at the same frame (numerically equal cores; checked in safe mode)'.

findings.title: GaussNewtonModel constructors do no structural validation of the sample/residual against the point; mismatches fail deep with obscure errors
findings.claim: apply_model / entries_model / probe_model (and the derivative kinds) accept ww and residual without checking len(ww) == d, ww[i].shape[-1] == N_i, or residual.shape == W + C; the mismatch surfaces later as an einsum label-size error, a bare IndexError, or a numpy broadcast error rather than a named structural error, contrary to the 'structural problems always error (at construction)' convention.
findings.evidence: apply_model(MANIFOLD, x, ww, r[:5]).gradient -> ValueError: Size of label 'c' for operand 2 (5) does not match previous terms (6); apply_model(MANIFOLD, x, ww[:2], r).gradient -> IndexError: list index out of range; a wrong Ni at mode 1 -> 'operands could not be broadcast together with remapped shapes'.
findings.repro_output:
apply_model residual wrong W (5 vs 6)   ValueError: Size of label 'c' for operand 2 (5) does not match previous terms (6).
apply_model ww wrong d (2 vectors)      IndexError: list index out of range
findings.proposed_fix: Validate the sample against the point's shape and the residual against the sample stack in the model constructors (or SamplingKind.precompute) with a named ValueError.
findings.supported_path: fitting.apply_model / probe_model / entries_model with a sample or residual of the wrong shape

findings.title: safety._inside_jax_trace: the primary detector (jax.core.trace_state_clean) does not exist in jax 0.10.2; docstring overstates what the probe fallback detects
findings.claim: jax.core.trace_state_clean is absent in the pinned jax 0.10.2, so every checks_active call on jax inputs raises and catches an AttributeError before falling back to the committed-array probe. The probe works under jit (including the closed-over concrete jax frame case, which was verified to compile), but the docstring's 'True iff we are inside any jax transform (jit / grad / vmap), independent of the inputs' is not what the probe delivers: under vmap or grad with concrete operands it returns False and the checks run (harmless, since the operands are concrete).
findings.evidence: hasattr(jax.core, 'trace_state_clean') = False (jax 0.10.2); _inside_jax_trace: eager False, in jit True; checks_active under jit with closed-over numpy/jax arrays = False; under vmap/grad with closed-over concrete arrays = True; jit(MANIFOLD.project) with a closed-over concrete jax frame: OK.
findings.repro_output:
jax 0.10.2 has trace_state_clean: False has Tracer: True
jit, closed-over jax    : False
vmap, closed-over numpy : [1. 1.]
_inside_jax_trace in jit: True
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the dead trace_state_clean path (or use the current public equivalent) so the probe is the single mechanism, and narrow the docstring to jit.

findings.title: d=1: MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame, T3) and MANIFOLD.transport raise IndexError
findings.claim: For a single-mode TuckerTensorTrain (d=1), tv_project_t3_onto_tangent_space calls tt_zipper_left_to_right(other_tt_cores2[:-1], left_tt_cores[:-1]) on empty tuples and indexes into them, so MANIFOLD.project_ambient(frame, <TuckerTensorTrain>), MANIFOLD.transport(v, new_frame), and project_ambient(frame, dense, method='t3svd') all crash with a bare IndexError. Every other d=1 op (sampling, jets, all transposes, retract, dense project_ambient, t3svd, arithmetic) passes the dense oracles, so d=1 is a supported ragged structure; the deferral ledger explicitly says ragged d=1 is fine.
findings.evidence: repro_d1_transport.py: `project_ambient(frame, T3) RAISES ... File t3toolbox/backend/tv_operations.py, line 402 ... IndexError: tuple index out of range`; `transport(v, frame) RAISES` (same path); `project_ambient(frame, dense) OK`; `retract(v) OK`. Sweep: 18 d1 rows fail (project_ambient_t3_vs_dense, project_ambient_t3svd_method, transport_identity, transport_vs_project_ambient for C in {(),(2,),(2,3)}, K in {(),(2,)}); all other 658 d1 checks pass.
findings.repro_output: project_ambient(frame, T3) RAISES IndexError: tuple index out of range (tv_operations.py:402 tt_zipper_left_to_right(other_tt_cores2[:-1], left_tt_cores[:-1])); transport(v, frame) RAISES; project_ambient(frame, dense) OK T3Tangent; retract(v) OK
findings.proposed_fix: Guard d=1 in tv_project_t3_onto_tangent_space (empty zippers → the single-core projection reduces to contracting the up factor and the one TT core), or route d=1 through the dense projection path; add a d=1 case to test_manifold's transport/project tests.

findings.title: ut3_orthogonal_representations / UT3Frame.from_ut3 / UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame return a non-orthogonal frame for non-minimal-rank UT3s
findings.claim: For a UniformTuckerTensorTrain whose ranks are structurally non-minimal (TT rank r_i > n_{i-1} r_{i-1} or tail r_{d-1} > n_{d-1}, e.g. (3,5,4),(2,3,2),(1,4,3,1) or the (1,2,3,1) tail case; or a share()-entered point with Tucker rank n_i > r_i r_{i+1}), ut3_orthogonal_representations squashes the masks but leaves the last left core / first right core far from orthonormal (||M^T M - I|| = 3.2e3; orthogonality_residual 0.14–1.0), with left ranks (1,2,2,1) inconsistent with right ranks (1,4,2,1). The frame still represents x (dense relerr 1e-15), so nothing upstream notices. In safe mode every subsequent UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.randn/project/retract/project_ambient raises 'requires an orthogonal frame ... Build the frame with UniformManifoldGeometry.frame' (which is exactly what was called); under safety.unsafe() or a jax trace the wrong frame is used silently. The ragged t3_orthogonal_representations on the same x is orthogonal (left ranks (1,2,3,1)), violating the uniform equivalence contract. Second facet: for randn((4,4,4),(2,2,2),(1,2,3,1)).share((0,0,0)) (shared-minimal ranks (4,4,4) but n0=4 > r0 r1=2), the padded ux.t3svd(sharing=) result is not left-orthogonal, the orth-rep residual is 1.0 (5e-7 unpadded), and uniform_fitting.uniform_minimal(ux, sharing) — the optimizers' guard — returns the same ranks and the same non-orthogonal frame, so the documented padded shared uniform restart runs on a non-orthogonal frame (silently under jit).

findings.title: 'retract stays a valid first-order retraction on a non-minimal frame' is false at numerically rank-deficient frames (the normal output of x.share(...))
findings.claim: docs/numerical_contracts.md:120 and docs/contributor/numerical_contract_catalog.md:144 (and the CLAUDE.md minimal-rank audit summary) state that MANIFOLD.retract is still a valid first-order retraction on a non-minimal frame and merely drops the numerically-redundant rank. At a frame that is numerically rank-deficient — which x.share(sharing) routinely produces (the group basis serves all group modes, so each mode's stored Tucker rank exceeds its numerical rank; frame.has_numerically_minimal_ranks is False) — the central-difference derivative of MANIFOLD.retract(h v) at 0 differs from v by a constant independent of h (4.7e-2 for share((0,0,0)) on (4,4,4); 1.1e-1 for share('aabb') on (5,5,4,4)) for h from 1e-2 down to 1e-5, i.e. the truncation drops O(h) mass of v in the deficient directions and the map is not first-order along those tangent directions. shared_manifold((0,0,0)).retract on the tied tangent shows the same constant 4.69e-2 (the 'aabb' shared retract is fine). Control cases — a structurally non-minimal but numerically full-rank frame (n0=4 > r0 r1=2) and a minimal frame — scale as h^2 as claimed. The sweep saw this as a constant FD error for every stack of the shall/sh4 structures (and sh2 at C=(2,3)).

'== share(aabb) ... ladder [1.09e-01 ×4]; shared_manifold ladder [1.82e-03, 1.85e-05, 1.85e-07, 1.89e-09]'. '== plain randn (5,5,4),(4,2,2),(1,2,2,1): n0=4 > r0*r1=2: has_minimal_ranks=False numerically minimal=False; ladder [1.11e-03, 1.12e-05, 1.12e-07, 1.08e-09]'. '== minimal control: [2.36e-05, 2.36e-07, 2.37e-09, 5.57e-10]'.
findings.proposed_fix: Narrow the caveat in numerical_contracts.md:120 / numerical_contract_catalog.md:144 to 'first-order on numerically full-rank frames; at a numerically rank-deficient frame the implicit truncation can drop O(h) mass of the step in the deficient directions', and cross-reference it from docs/sharing.md (share() produces such points; the padded-restart story should say the step is only partially taken until the rank fills).

findings.title: Safe-mode GAUGE check uses the relative tolerance as an absolute bound on an unnormalized residual: false failures for large tangents and for jax float32
findings.claim: ManifoldGeometry.inner/norm (and the uniform twins) pass safety.effective_rtol (documented as rtol: 1e-9 numpy, 1e-5 jax) as atol= to T3Tangent.is_gauged, which tests gauge_residual <= atol where gauge_residual is the unnormalized max-abs of U^T V / L^T H and therefore scales with the tangent's magnitude. A tangent the library itself just gauged with MANIFOLD.project fails the check once it is large (numpy float64, |p| ~ 5e7) and, on jax default float32, already at |p| ~ 54 -- which breaks the 'jax-but-not-jit usage in safe mode' that the two-tolerance design exists to support (CLAUDE.md). is_orthogonal is unaffected (orthonormal cores are O(1)).
findings.evidence: gauge_tol_scaling.py (numpy float64): scale 1e4 -> residual 2.2e-10 OK; scale 1e6 -> |p|=5.45e7, gauge_residual=1.49e-8 > atol 1e-9, is_gauged()=False, MANIFOLD.norm and MANIFOLD.inner RAISE 'requires gauged variations'. f32_safe_mode.py (jax float32, no x64): randn((4,5,6),(2,3,2),(1,2,2,1)) -> project ok, gauge_residual=1.16e-5 > 1e-5 -> MANIFOLD.norm RAISES; (6,7,8,5) -> residual 7.3e-4; UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.norm fails identically; with x64 all pass.
findings.repro_output: scale 1e+06: |p| = 5.45e+07, gauge_residual = 1.49e-08 (atol used = 1e-09), is_gauged() = False / MANIFOLD.norm RAISED: ManifoldGeometry.norm requires gauged variations ... ||| float32: project ok; gauge_residual = 1.1566e-05 ... MANIFOLD.norm FAILED: ValueError ManifoldGeometry.norm requires gauged variations
findings.proposed_fix: Make the gauge residual relative (normalize by the norms of the paired cores, or compare against rtol * |U||V|) in tv_gauge_residual / is_gauged, or rename the tolerance to atol and scale it per dtype; same for the uniform twin.
findings.supported_path: MANIFOLD.norm(MANIFOLD.project(v)) / MANIFOLD.inner in default safe mode, numpy float64 with large-magnitude data or jax default float32 (documented use).
findings.related_known: CLAUDE.md 'Two tolerances' paragraph (rtol_jax supports jax-but-not-jit safe mode); docs/contributor/numerical_contract_catalog.md

findings.title: Uniform orthogonal frame is NOT orthogonal for numerically rank-deficient trains (zero-padded resize warm starts, x + x); ragged twin is orthonormal
findings.claim: ut3_orthogonal_representations / UT3Frame.from_ut3 / UNIFORM_MANIFOLD.frame produce a frame with exact-zero slices inside real mask slots (orthogonality residual 1.0) whenever the input has vanishing singular values -- e.g. the zero-padded x.resize(...) warm start that docs/rank_continuation.md:161-180 prescribes for uniform rank continuation (UT3.from_t3(x.resize(...)) then newton_cg(UNIFORM_MANIFOLD,...)), or x + x. The ragged t3_orthogonal_representations on the same input gives residual ~1e-15. In safe mode the uniform project/project_ambient/transport raise 'requires an orthogonal frame' on a frame the library built; the optimizer path never checks, so newton_cg silently optimizes in a smaller tangent space (missing the zero-column directions). Given the SAME frame the ragged and uniform projections agree to 2e-16 and equal the dense LS projection, so the defect is in the uniform frame construction, not the projection.
findings.evidence: uniform_rankdef_frame.py: x.resize zero-padded (3,3,3)/(1,3,3,1), has_minimal_ranks=True: ragged frame residual 6.7e-16, uniform 1.0e+00; unsafe project_ambient ragged-vs-uniform rel diff 3.59e-01; safe mode RAISES. uniform_rankdef_apples.py: converted uniform frame has zero slices in down[1],down[2],left[2],right[0],right[1]; same-frame projections agree 2e-16. uniform_resized_x0_fit.py: newton_cg from the same x0, objective after 4 Newton steps 6.05e4 (ragged) vs 8.08e4 (uniform), no error raised. uniform_stacked_frame.py: stacked (2,) x+x -> is_orthogonal [True False].

findings.proposed_fix: In the uniform up/down/left/right sweep keep the full orthonormal U from the SVD for the masked-real slots regardless of ss==0 (complete the basis as the ragged path does), or shrink the masks to the numerical rank when singular values vanish; add a garbage/zero-padded-input test for ut3_orthogonal_representations per testing_strategy.md.

findings.title: stacking.stack (T3/T3Frame/T3Variations/T3Tangent/UT3 stack) is not jittable: xnp.arange used as static moveaxis source
findings.claim: stacking.stack calls xnp.moveaxis(stacked, source=xnp.arange(len(axes)), destination=axes). findings.title: 29 assert-guarded structural checks vanish under python -O: corewise ops silently truncate, T3 * wrong-shape array silently broadcasts
findings.claim: Structural consistency is enforced by assert(...) at 29 sites (corewise.py:61,62,84,85,210,211,241,242; backend/ranks.py:111,112,342,353,354,537,538; backend/t3_linalg.py:61,117,195,258; backend/t3_operations.py:296,297; backend/common.py:346,352,369,375,390,396; backend/probing.py:1514,1515; tucker_tensor_train.py:2023). Under python -O these are stripped, contradicting the house rule that structural problems always error: corewise_add/sub/dot on length-mismatched trees return a silently truncated result (zip), and x * ndarray of the wrong shape returns a broadcast dense array; others degrade to IndexError/ValueError from numpy. Without -O they raise a bare AssertionError with no message.
findings.evidence: asserts_under_O.py: without -O every case -> AssertionError (empty message); with -O: corewise_add len mismatch -> RETURNED tuple len 2 (inputs had 3 vs 2 elements); corewise_dot len mismatch -> RETURNED float64; x * np.ones((4,5,1)) -> RETURNED (4,5,6) ndarray; t3_sum axis=5 -> IndexError; compute_minimal_ranks bad tt len -> IndexError; t3_add stack mismatch -> numpy ValueError.

findings.proposed_fix: Replace the structural assert(...) calls with explicit raise ValueError(message) (they are cheap integer/shape checks).

findings.title: jax absent: randn(use_jax=True) is a bare NameError (beyond get_backend); to_jax()/load(use_jax=True) silently return numpy

findings.title: Stacked t3_orthogonal_representations rotates the t3svd Tucker factors, so T3FrameWeights.from_t3weights(T3Weights.from_t3svd(x)) is applied in the wrong gauge (docs/weighting.md recipe)
findings.claim: The weighting page pairs frame, _ = t3_orthogonal_representations(x) with W = T3FrameWeights.from_t3weights(T3Weights.from_t3svd(x)); the sigma-weights are per-coordinate in the t3svd gauge. For an unstacked t3svd output the re-orthogonalized frame's up cores equal the t3svd factors up to sign, but for stack_shape=(2,) they do not (the stacked sweep rotates the Tucker factors), so the sigma-weights land on rotated coordinates; this surfaces as the absorbed tangent differing between numpy and jax on identical input (relerr 0.7 ragged d2 (2,); 0.09/1.4 uniform d2 ()), i.e. the weighted result is gauge-dependent on a path the docs present as canonical.
findings.evidence: inline check (lane log): stack () -> frame up cores == t3svd tucker cores up to sign: numpy True jax True; stack (2,) -> False False (numpy vs jax frames identical). matrix_ragged_tangent.out: TANGENT d2 (2,) tangent_absorb_weights np/jax MISMATCH relerr 7.04e-01; matrix_uniform.out: UNIFORM d2 () tangent_absorb_weights MISMATCH 9.26e-02, ufv_absorb_weights MISMATCH 1.41e+00.
findings.repro_output: stack (2,) | numpy vs jax frames identical: True | frame up cores == t3svd tucker cores up to sign: numpy False jax False ||| TANGENT d2 (2,) tangent_absorb_weights np/jax MISMATCH relerr 7.04e-01
findings.proposed_fix: Document that from_t3svd weights pair with the t3svd gauge and build the frame with T3Frame.from_t3(xs) (no re-orthogonalization) in that recipe; or make t3_orthogonal_representations leave already-orthonormal Tucker factors untouched (stacked path included). To confirm fully: compare weighted_norm against the dense sigma-weighted norm for a stacked xs.
findings.supported_path: docs/weighting.md lines 79-82 recipe applied to a stacked (C != ()) point, or to a uniform point.
findings.related_known: docs/contributor/weighted_internals.md (weights batch with the frame)

findings.title: adam on a ragged MANIFOLD x0 with non-minimal ranks crashes at step 2 with a bare broadcast error
findings.claim: The Adam moment trees m/v are allocated once with corewise_zeros_like(cores) at x0's core shapes. On the ragged MANIFOLD geometry a non-minimal-rank x0 (e.g. d=2 (4,5)/(2,3)/(1,2,1), where n_1=3 > r_1*r_2=2, or d=3 (2,3,2)/(1,2,1,1)) has its redundant rank dropped by the first retraction (the documented caveat), so the second step's corewise_map(m, g) sees mismatched core shapes and raises 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)'. newton_cg, gradient_descent and mc_sgd rebuild everything per step and run fine from the same x0 (ranks drop to minimal); the uniform path reduces x0 transparently via uniform_minimal in _setup, but the ragged _setup branch (t3toolbox/optimizers.py:193-203) does not.
findings.evidence: repro_nonminimal_ragged.py: 'x0 ranks (2, 3) (1, 2, 1) minimal: ((2, 2), (1, 2, 1)) has_minimal_ranks: False / newton_cg OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1) / gradient_descent OK / mc_sgd OK / adam RAISED ValueError operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)'; from the minimal-reduced x0 (same tensor) adam runs. sweep_misc.out 'x0 variants' shows the d=3 analogue: 'EXC nonminimal ragged adam: ValueError ... (3,5) (2,5)' while 'OK nonminimal uniform adam'.
findings.repro_output:
newton_cg OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
gradient_descent OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
mc_sgd OK ranks -> (2, 2) (1, 2, 1)
adam RAISED ValueError operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (3,5) (2,5)
reduced x0 ranks (2, 2) (1, 2, 1) same tensor: True
newton_cg from minimal x0 OK
findings.proposed_fix: Reduce a ragged x0 to minimal ranks in the ragged branch of optimizers._setup (mirror of uniform_minimal: t3svd + rank_adjustment_sweep('right_to_left')), or in backend adam re-allocate m/v with corewise_zeros_like when the retracted core shapes change; at minimum reject a non-minimal ragged x0 with a clear message.
findings.supported_path: topt.adam(t3m.MANIFOLD, 'apply', ww, b, x0, rng, batch) with any TuckerTensorTrain x0 whose ranks are not minimal (e.g. TuckerTensorTrain.randn((4,5),(2,3),(1,2,1))); the docstring says 'x0: initial point (any cores; the geometry orthogonalizes internally)' and docs/fitting_and_optimization.md claims 4 optimizers x 2 geometries.
findings.related_known: Retract's non-minimal-frame 'caveat' (docs/numerical_contracts.md:120) is the mechanism; the uniform-only minimal reduction is documented at backend/uniform_fitting.py:351 ('The ragged layer tolerates non-minimal ranks').
findings.lane: O2 — oracle sweep: fitting and optimizers

findings.title: adam on MANIFOLD is gauge-dependent: numpy-eager, jax-eager, jit, ragged and uniform give different iterates
findings.claim: Adam accumulates m/v in the coordinates of the current orthonormal frame, which on MANIFOLD is re-chosen every step by an SVD whose sign/gauge convention differs between numpy and jax and between the ragged and uniform orthogonalizations; nothing transports the moments, so the iterate is not a function of the point. The same adam call therefore returns results differing at the 3e-3..4e-2 level between numpy-eager and jax-eager (no jit involved), eager and jit, and ragged and uniform, while adam on COREWISE and every other optimizer on MANIFOLD agree to ~1e-15. This contradicts docs/fitting_and_optimization.md:14 ('4 optimizers x 2 geometries ... no combinatorial code') and :288-290 ('a single kernel runs numpy-eager, jax-eager, or jit-compiled') for this cell; adam's docstrings only say COREWISE is 'intended'.
findings.evidence: repro_adam_manifold_gauge.py (x64, 50 Adam steps, apply, d=3): 'MANIFOLD: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 5.7e-03 | vs jit 6.5e-03 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 6.9e-03 / COREWISE: 2.5e-16 | 4.6e-16 | 1.6e-16 / newton_cg MANIFOLD: eager vs jit 7.2e-15, ragged vs uniform 5.8e-15'. sweep_misc.out: every MANIFOLD and shared-MANIFOLD row (ragged and uniform, all kinds, with/without reg) shows adam eager-vs-jit 2e-3..4e-2 while newton_cg/mc_sgd are <6e-14; all COREWISE rows OK to 1e-15.
findings.repro_output:
MANIFOLD: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 5.7e-03 | vs jit 6.5e-03 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 6.9e-03
COREWISE: ragged numpy-eager vs jax-eager 2.5e-16 | vs jit 4.6e-16 | ragged vs uniform (numpy) 1.6e-16
newton_cg MANIFOLD: eager vs jit 7.2e-15, ragged vs uniform 5.8e-15
findings.proposed_fix: Document in adam's backend+frontend docstrings and in docs/fitting_and_optimization.md §2.4/§4.5 that on MANIFOLD the moments are not transported, so results depend on the frame gauge (backend- and layer-dependent) and adam should be used with COREWISE; alternatively warn/raise on a manifold geometry, or transport/reset m and v each step.
findings.supported_path: topt.adam(t3m.MANIFOLD or ut3m.UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, kind, sample, data, x0, rng, batch[, use_jit=True]) — accepted by the signature ('COREWISE (intended) / MANIFOLD (must match x0)').
findings.lane: O2 — oracle sweep: fitting and optimizers

findings.title: GaussNewtonModel.jacobian return comment and residual field comment omit the uniform PACKED layout
findings.claim: The jacobian return shape comment says 'probe: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,)' and the residual field comment (line 265) says 'len=d, W+C+(Ni,) (probe)', but for a uniform model both are the packed zero-padded ndarray (d,)+W+C+(N,) (and (d,)+(order+1,)+W+C+(N,) for probe_derivatives). Only the sample field comment mentions '(uniform: PACKED)'. A user following the comment (e.g. zipping the jacobian with a ragged residual list) hits a broadcast error — exactly how my driver first failed.
findings.evidence: repro_small_docs.py: 'ragged jacobian (probe): tuple [(12, 4), (12, 5), (12, 6)] / uniform jacobian (probe): ndarray (3, 12, 6) (docstring: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,)) / uniform residual field: ndarray (3, 12, 6)'. The padding is verified zero in sweep_models.py (check packed_pad_zero, 0 failures).
findings.repro_output:
ragged jacobian (probe): tuple [(12, 4), (12, 5), (12, 6)]
uniform jacobian (probe): ndarray (3, 12, 6)  (docstring: len=d, elm_shape=W+C+(Ni,))
uniform residual field: ndarray (3, 12, 6) (field comment: len=d, W+C+(Ni,) (probe))
findings.proposed_fix: Add the uniform packed form to the jacobian return comment and the residual field comment ('uniform: PACKED (d,)+[(order+1,)]+W+C+(N,), zero-padded'), matching the existing '(uniform: PACKED)' note on sample.
findings.supported_path: fitting.probe_model(ut3m.UNIFORM_MANIFOLD, UniformTuckerTensorTrain, ww, r).jacobian(p)

findings.title: gradient_descent has no use_jit and its docstring does not say so
findings.claim: topt.gradient_descent accepts chunk_size= but no use_jit=; passing use_jit=True is forwarded through **kwargs to the backend and fails with 'TypeError: gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument use_jit'. The module docstring (line 24) correctly scopes use_jit to mc_sgd/adam/newton_cg, but the function docstring never mentions it, so the error is the only cue.
findings.evidence: repro_small_docs.py: gradient_descent(use_jit=True): TypeError gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_jit'
findings.repro_output: gradient_descent(use_jit=True): TypeError gradient_descent() got an unexpected keyword argument 'use_jit'
findings.proposed_fix: One-line note in gradient_descent's docstring (eager only; use_jit is on mc_sgd/adam/newton_cg), or accept use_jit and raise a clear ValueError.
findings.related_known: Flagged as a docstring gap in the sampling/optimization map §3 (kwargs check).
findings.lane: O2 — oracle sweep: fitting and optimizers
